TL;DR: Mortgage rates went up today, but they're still in a much better place than this time last month.

Mortgage rates are higher today, but only by a little. And they're still hovering below 7%, which is much better than what we saw around this time last month.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage ticked up to 6.98% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is two basis points higher than Friday and five basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.)

Mortgage rates have more room to rise, as a stronger-than-expected jobs report reinforced expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike in December.

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:

As for what’s next: Tomorrow’s jobs report, showing October data, could potentially nudge mortgage rates in either direction. To understand the link between jobs data and mortgage rates, keep reading below the video.

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

This week, the Nerds are watching the October Consumer Price Index, which comes out on Tuesday. CPI is one of two key measures of inflation, which the Federal Reserve aims to keep in check relative to the strength of the labor market. (The Fed looks more closely at a different inflation measure, the Personal Consumption Expenditures Index, which comes out Nov. 25.)

Right now, the labor market is looking pretty darn strong: The October jobs report, released Friday from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, showed U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, far more than economists expected, and unemployment edged down to 4.1%.

Raising the federal funds rate is the Fed’s main tool for bringing inflation down, but rate hikes are only on the table when the labor market is strong enough to handle it. Considering Friday’s jobs data, it’s looking fairly likely that the Fed will approve a rate hike when the committee meets Dec. 8-9. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates directly, but an anticipated rate hike can put upward pressure on mortgage rates, which respond to investors’ expectations for the economy and Fed policy.

Still, a jump in mortgage rates isn’t a sure thing, and market sentiment could shift over the next month. October’s inflation data will capture the effect of the Fed’s last rate hike, which came in the middle of September. If that worked as intended and inflation shows signs of slowing, mortgage rates might remain around 7%.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.48% or higher.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

» Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

» Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis

If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

#3092. Coinbase net income surges 66% in third quarter, benefiting from bitcoin investment gains

Coinbase Global earned third-quarter adjusted net income of $719 million, up 66% from $433 million a year ago, largely due to a recovery in the cryptocurrency market.

Coinbase said it earned $2.51 a share in the latest quarter, although it wasn't immediately clear if that compared with the 6-cent-per-share profit that Wall Street analysts had estimated. Revenue of $1.20 billion trailed the $1.233 billion expected by analysts polled by LSEG.

Net income at the San Francisco-based platform surged thanks to the value of its volatile cryptocurrency investment portfolio, which can swing wildly even when the composition of the underlying holdings are little changed.

The third quarter value of Coinbase's crypto investment portfolio climbed due to a resurgence in the digital asset market. The price of bitcoin — often used as a gauge for all crypto assets — rose 39% in the three-month period ended Sept. 30 and the flagship cryptocurrency recently changed hands at roughly $80,809.

In the third quarter, Coinbase deepened its push into non-crypto products and services, including artificial intelligence integrations for traders, tokenized real-world assets and prediction markets.

In July, VP of product Max Branzburg told CNBC that Coinbase would debut an "everything exchange" spotlighting tokenized stocks and other real-world assets, derivatives trading, prediction markets and early-stage token sales. The trading platform also introduced Coinbase for Agents in early October, supporting users that want to use ChatGPT, Muse or other AI agents to manage their portfolios or research and trade various assets.

Coinbase also expanded its prediction market offerings, making a wider range of event contracts available to users.

In the third quarter, prediction markets revenue grew to more than $200 million on an annual basis, while the number of traders on those markets increased 60% compared with the second quarter.

#3091. Myomo (MYO) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Record orders and a sharp margin jump signal a shift toward professional referrals.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Myomo, Inc. (MYO +15.70%) reported record quarterly revenue and reached approximately breakeven adjusted EBITDA as it continues a strategic transition toward recurring professional referral sources. Management indicated that the MyoConnect program, which now spans more than 500 locations, is driving a higher percentage of revenue from clinical referrals while reducing the relative cost of customer acquisition. The company reported significant gross margin expansion driven by material cost reductions and higher manufacturing volumes. Management stated that new commercial leadership and expanded payer network access are expected to support continued scale across the United States and Germany.

Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Myomo's Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. Should you need assistance, After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Please note this event is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Vivian Cervantes, Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Paul R. Gudonis: Thank you, operator, and good afternoon, everyone. This is Vivian Cervantes with Alliance Advisors IR. Welcome to Myomo's third quarter 2026 financial results conference call. With me today are Myomo's Chief Executive Officer, Paul R. Gudonis and Chief Financial Officer, David A. Henry. Before we begin, I would like to caution listeners that statements made during this call by management, other than historical facts are forward looking statements. The words anticipate, believe, estimate, expect, intend, guidance, outlook, confidence, target, project, and other similar expressions are typically used to identify such forward looking statements.

These forward looking statements are not guarantees of future performance and may involve and are subject to risks and uncertainties and other factors that may affect Myomo's business financial condition and operating results. These risks, uncertainties and other factors are discussed in Myomo's filings with the SEC, Actual outcomes and results may differ materially from what is expressed in or implied by these forward looking statements. Furthermore, except as required by law, Myomo undertakes no obligation to revise or update any forward looking statements to reflect events or circumstances after the date of this call today, November 9, 2026. Now my pleasure to turn the call over to Myomo's CEO, Paul R. Gudonis. Paul, please go ahead.

David A. Henry: Thanks, Vivian, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you all for joining us today. Myomo's purpose is to help people living with chronic arm and hand paralysis to regain function and independence with our powered arm braces. In the third quarter we made progress in reaching more of these patients we serve, while improving the economics of our business. Revenue reached a quarterly record of $12.3 million up 22% from a year ago Gross margin rose to 71.3%, and we delivered approximately breakeven adjusted EBITDA.

Paul R. Gudonis: These results reflect continued execution on the 4 success pillars we discussed on our last call including building recurring patient sources, expanding payer access, demonstrating operating leverage and investing in product development and clinical research. Let me walk through the progress on each. The first success pillar relates to increasing revenue from recurring patient sources. Patients referred from rehab hospitals and stroke clinics, orthotics and prosthetics partners and the VA represented 54% of third quarter revenue compared with 33% a year ago. This reflects the success of our MyoConnect program which is now entering its second year.

Since its launch healthcare professionals at more than 500 rehabilitation facilities and therapy centers have referred potential MyoPro patients to us which is an increase of over 200 locations in the past quarter. That milestone gives us a broader base of relationships which patients can learn about the device during their care enables us to build a more durable business over time versus relying solely on direct to patient marketing. We see a growing number of physicians and therapists recommending a Myo Pro for their patients and we expect a larger number of referrals per facility as they see the benefits of the MyoPro for their patients.

We are already seeing this same store sales growth of over 30%, as our recent referrals came from the existing sites, the therapists and physicians that know our company, the product line, the clinical research that is been published, and their patients' good outcomes with the MyoPro. The increase in referring locations contributed to the record number of orders in the quarter which came in at 258 in the third quarter. Our success pillar number 2 is to increase market access so that more qualified patients can obtain a MyoPro. During the quarter, we have either entered into agreements or in the process of finalizing agreements with payers that covered an additional 35 million lives.

For the payers with contracts that have been completed, we are in the process of going live, as an in network provider. These agreements include the payers Medicare Advantage and commercial plans. We also made progress with state Medicaid agencies where we are now enrolled with 7 states such as Pennsylvania, Michigan, and Wisconsin. We have other state Medicaid plans in the queue This will help us with patients that have Medicaid in these states, subject to individual medical coverage policies plus the ability to receive secondary insurance payments for our Medicare patients who may reside in these states.

Our plan is to continue to enter into more such contracts given our track record of a higher pre authorization rate from the MyoPro when we are an in network provider. Our third success pillar is generating operating leverage. Our target is to grow revenues at least twice as fast as operating expenses. We achieved that goal again in the third quarter as revenue grew 22% year over year, while operating expenses grew just 6%. In addition, gross margin improved by 750 basis points in the third quarter compared with the prior year.

We are continuing our path to profitability and sustainable positive cash flow by working on additional cost savings such as the in sourcing of 3D printing of the custom fabricated shells for each MyoPro, which should go online by the end of this year. Our efficiency efforts in the other functional areas are also making a financial impact with our overall volumes up while our headcount is down over the past 2 years. Our fourth success pillar is continued progress with product development and clinical research.

The randomized control trial at the University of Utah continues to make steady progress with 35 of the planned 50 subjects now enrolled up from 25 at the time of our second quarter call Development work also continued on the MyoPro 3 and on the hand only product for the German market. These efforts are a part of our longer term work to expand the evidence base and the applications of our wearable robotics platform. We will provide further updates as milestones are reached. In summary, the quarter showed how executing across our 4 pillars of success reinforce 1 another.

More referral relationships and payer access helped drive record orders and revenue, higher volume, and cost reduction supported stronger gross margin and improved operating performance. We are building on our market leading position by investing in the clinical, commercial and product capabilities needed to serve more patients. To continue scaling our commercial operations, last month we announced that Mary-Katherine McClure has joined Myomo as our new Chief Commercial Officer. She has a successful track record of growing revenues establishing strong referral partnerships and leading a sales and field clinical team from our experience at fast growing Inspire Medical and other medical device companies.

I am pleased to have her bring this experience to Myomo as we execute our plan to further address this large unmet need of chronic arm paralysis in the country. With that overview, I will turn the call over to David A. Henry to review our financial results in greater detail.

David A. Henry: Thank you, Paul, and good afternoon, everyone. Our revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was a record $12.3 million up 22% versus the prior year period. The increase was driven by both a higher average selling price or ASP and a higher number of revenue units. ASP for the quarter was approximately $55.5 thousand up about 2% versus the prior year And we recognized revenue on a record 222 MyoPro units, an increase of 19% over the third quarter of 2025. Looking at payer mix, Medicare Part B patients represented 54% of both third quarter revenue and prior year period revenue. Medicare Advantage plans represented 17% of third quarter revenue compared with 18% in the second quarter of 2025.

Our transition toward recurring patient sources continued to accelerate during the quarter. Recurring patient sources represented 54% of third quarter revenue compared with 33% in the prior year quarter. Within those recurring channels, 27% of total revenue was generated by direct billing referrals, through our MyoConnect program up from 23% in the second quarter and 20% in the first quarter of 2026. We continue to see strong results from our other recurring channels: international revenue representing 17% of revenue and U. S. O and P revenue representing 8% of revenue, VA patients represented 2% of revenue in the third quarter. Turning to our metrics, we received a record 258 MyoPro orders during the quarter, up 13% year-over-year.

We added 600 patients to the pipeline during the quarter, down compared with the second quarter of 2026. MyoConnect referrals represented 18% of pipeline adds in the third quarter. Third quarter MyoConnect pipeline adds were influenced by seasonality in the third quarter from summer vacations among referring sources as well as temporary internal staffing constraints. Staffing constraints have been alleviated entering the fourth quarter. Our direct to patient advertising spending was up 2% year-over-year Advertising driven pipeline ads in the quarter were impacted by an inefficiency in our lead generation, which resulted in fewer workable leads a lower conversion rate among those generated in the quarter.

We continually test new methodologies for patient targeting in order to maximize spend effectiveness and optimize customer acquisition cost. With the aforementioned MyoConnect resource constraints alleviated, and the implementation of improvements in direct-to-patient lead generation we generated approximately 30% more direct billing pipeline ads in October than the per month average in the third quarter. We ended the quarter with a backlog of 217 patients, down modestly from the second quarter as the efficiency of our operations turned record orders in the quarter into a record number of revenue units. Turning to our financial results. Gross margin in the second quarter was 71.3%, up from 63.8% in the prior year quarter.

The improvement was driven primarily by the higher ASP, material cost reductions and the spreading of fixed costs over a higher number of revenue units, partially offset by somewhat higher clinical costs we classified the cost of goods sold. Operating expenses were 10.5 million representing an increase of 6% compared with the third quarter of 2025. Higher general and administrative expenses and R&D was tempered by lower sales, clinical and marketing spending in the quarter. Operating loss improved significantly to 1.7 million compared with $3.5 million in the prior year quarter. We achieved adjusted EBITDA breakeven in the third quarter, compared with a loss of $2.7 million a year ago.

We are keenly focused on operating leverage and minimizing cash burn as we carefully invest in MyoConnect. Note that a portion of the improvement in adjusted EBITDA is due to higher stock based compensation expense, as certain employee incentive payments were paid in stock during the third quarter as part of our cash management initiatives. We expect stock based compensation expense to return to its typical run rate in the fourth quarter. Below operating loss, second quarter results include a noncash charge of approximately $1.8 million related to a market adjustment for the valuation of our derivative liabilities, as well as cash and non cash interest expense associated with the Avenue Capital term loan.

Including the aforementioned non cash charge net loss for the third quarter was $4.2 million or $0.10 per share compared with $3.7 million or $0.09 per share in the third quarter of 2025. Turning now to our balance sheet and cash flow. As of September 30, 2026, cash, cash equivalents and short term investments was $11.9 million. Cash used in operating activities during the second quarter was $1.3 million compared with $1.8 million used during the third quarter of 2025. Cash burn or the change in cash in the quarter was $1.5 million an improvement from $2.2 million in the second quarter.

Let me conclude with our outlook Last quarter, we raised our full year guidance to a range of $45 million to $47 million We are narrowing that guidance today to $46 million to $47 million at the upper end of that previous range. We expect that the beneficial effect of manufacturing cost reduction initiatives will result in a modest sequential increase in gross margin in the fourth quarter. 1 time costs associated with the transition of our Chief Commercial Officer and higher headcount in support of our MyoConnect program is expected to result in a modest sequential increase in operating expenses in the fourth quarter.

Despite this expected increase, are maintaining our previously communicated operating leverage objective of limiting the growth of operating expenses in all of 2026 to half the rate of 2026 revenue growth. We continue to expect total cash burn in the second half of the year to be less than $2 million or less than $500 thousand in the fourth quarter. Overall, we are pleased that we are poised to meet or exceed financial and operating objectives for 2026. And we look forward to continued execution in 2027. With that financial overview, I will turn the call back to Paul.

Paul R. Gudonis: Thanks, David. Well, to summarize over the past year, we have executed on all 4 of our success pillars to grow Myomo at volume and revenues while improving key financial metrics including gross margin, adjusted EBITDA and cash usage. In September, I attended the American Orthotics and Prosthetics Association National Conference where we met with new and existing O&P partners to establish a deeper engagement with this channel so that they can have another product included in their treatment plans for their stroke patients.

As an example of how these relationships are working, 1 of the national providers recently brought our MyoConnect clinicians into 1 of their possible referral sources which resulted in several patients added to their candidate pipeline and delivery of their first MyoPro to a patient who is now able to use their arm and hand again for the first time in years. We look forward to replicating these successes in our markets in the US and Germany, as we have a very large opportunity in front of us to improve the lives of many individuals with our proprietary technology.

We have established Myomo as the market leader with over 4 thousand devices provided to patients with paralysis And yet this is only about 1% penetration of the addressable market. Over 3 million individuals in the US suffer from chronic arm paralysis and another 250 thousand cases that result from the 800 thousand strokes that occur annually in the US.

We have already laid the foundation for executing our strategy of continued market penetration and revenue growth by hiring additional field clinical staff across the US and Germany to develop more referral relationships with the physicians and therapists that treat these patients And this evolution of our go to market strategy will lead to a growing, durable business serving this patient population for years to come. Now Dave and I are ready to take your questions. Operator.

Operator: While we are waiting for the first question, I would like to mention that next week, we will be in the Craig-Hallum's 17th Annual Alpha Select Conference in New York on November 17. David and I along with our new Chief Commercial Officer Mary-Katherine McClure will attend in person at this conference and will be available for 1-on-1 meetings. #3089. Public Policy (PPHC) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Acquisitions and client demand lifted results as full-year outlook held.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Public Policy Holding Company, Inc. (PPHC -0.90%) reported year-to-date revenue growth of 15.2%, driven by a combination of organic expansion in its core government relations business and the integration of four strategic acquisitions. Management indicated that political transitions at federal and state levels serve as catalysts for client demand, as corporate interests navigate new regulatory agendas and institutional changes. The company maintained its full-year 2026 financial outlook while expanding its capital capacity through a new senior credit facility to support further geographic and service-line expansion. Segment performance varied, with government relations exhibiting margin expansion while corporate communications faced temporary headwinds related to the election cycle.

#3087. Hain Celestial (HAIN) Q1 2027 Earnings Call Transcript

A missed lender deadline clouds Hain Celestial's pending $323 million international sale.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

The Hain Celestial Group, Inc. (HAIN -6.56%) reported its fiscal first quarter 2027 results and updated its strategic progress, including receiving final regulatory approvals for the $323 million sale of its international business to Aurelius. Management stated that the company is pursuing a path forward for the divestiture despite missing an October deadline to secure a necessary credit agreement amendment. The company reported a significant increase in North American gross margins to 33.5% following the exit of its snacks business and the implementation of productivity initiatives. Management stated that the go-forward portfolio will concentrate on core brands including The Greek Gods, Celestial Seasonings, and Earth's Best as part of a more streamlined operating model.

Please refer to our most recent annual report on Form 10-K, our annual report on Form 10-K expected to be filed today, our quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, and our other reports filed from time to time with the SEC, as well as the press release issued this morning for a detailed discussion of the risks. We have also prepared a presentation inclusive of additional supplemental financial information, which is posted on our website at hain.com under the Investors heading. As we discuss our results today, unless noted as reported, our remarks will focus on non-GAAP or adjusted financial measures.

Reconciliations of non-GAAP financial measures to GAAP results are available in the earnings release and the slide presentation accompanying this call. This call is being webcast and an archive will be made available on the website. Now I'd like to turn the call over to Alison.

Alison Lewis: Thank you, Alexis. Good morning, everyone, and thank you all for joining the call today. Fiscal Year 2026 was a pivotal year for Hain. Over the past 12 months, we took decisive actions to simplify our portfolio, pay down debt, improve execution, drive greater cost discipline, and sharpen our strategic focus. While there is more work ahead, we are exiting the year with improving momentum, stronger cash generation, and a clear plan to drive growth and profitability in the go-forward business. Earlier today, we announced that we reached a definitive agreement to sell our international business to a private equity firm, Aurelius, for $323 million in cash.

This transaction would represent an important step in the evolution of Hain, and when coupled with the fiscal Q3 divestiture of our North American snacks business, would mark a significant milestone in the simplification and strengthening of our portfolio. We believe we found a strong home for our international business in Aurelius, and I want to thank our international employees for their dedication, passion, and contributions to Hain over many years. They have built remarkable brands, which we are confident will thrive under the new ownership. The sale is expected to be completed in our fiscal second quarter, and proceeds from the transaction would be used to further reduce debt.

As noted in our announcement, the transaction is conditioned upon securing an amendment for our credit agreement to extend the maturity, and we remain in active discussions with our lenders regarding that amendment. Once the transaction is closed, the resulting portfolio would be a North American business comprised of leading brands in attractive categories with a more streamlined operating model and a greater focus on core growth opportunities. Importantly, the strength of this portfolio was demonstrated in our fourth quarter results. North America returned to organic sales growth, expanded gross margin by nearly 1,200 basis points, and increased adjusted EBITDA by 55% year-over-year. These results reflect the benefits of a streamlined portfolio, stronger execution, productivity initiatives, and disciplined cost management.

Looking forward, the simplified portfolio will allow us to concentrate our resources and management attention on the areas where we see the greatest potential to create value. Fiscal 2026 also marked a year of substantial balance sheet improvement. We reduced net debt by $151 million through a combination of actions resulting from our strategic review and strong free cash flow generation of $58 million. This free cash flow improvement was driven by a number of factors, including tighter working capital management, meaningful inventory reduction, productivity initiatives, and disciplined cost control. These factors not only drove cash generation in the year but strengthened our operational foundation.

The international transaction would further reduce debt significantly and position us to continue the ongoing transformation of our portfolio and capital structure. Our focus will now shift to simplifying the organization and aligning our cost structure with the scale of the future North America business to drive growth and profitability. Turning now to our performance. As I mentioned earlier, we exited fiscal 2026 with improved momentum across many areas of the business. Additionally, we made significant progress against our strategic priorities, including portfolio simplification, debt reduction, cash generation, and operational improvement. During the quarter, we delivered sequential improvement in organic net sales growth across the business as our five actions to win continued to gain traction across the organization.

These actions include simplifying our portfolio, accelerating renovation and innovation, implementing strategic revenue growth management, driving productivity and working capital efficiency, and strengthening our digital capabilities. Importantly, we see measurable results from these initiatives. Our innovation renewal rate, or IRR, expanded year-over-year in both North America and international to a high single digit and low teen percentage, respectively, for fiscal 2026. IRR is a measure of the percent of net sales coming from new or relaunched SKUs in the last three years and a strong validation that our innovation is delivering results. E-commerce sales delivered strong double-digit growth in Q4 year-over-year with our largest pure-play and omni-channel customers in North America, reflecting the progress of our digital transformation initiatives.

Productivity efforts in supply chain continue to deliver substantial COGS reduction. While the environment remains dynamic and challenges persist in certain categories, these results reinforce our confidence that the actions we are taking are beginning to strengthen the business and build the foundation for future growth. In North America, organic net sales returned to growth in Q4, increasing 2% year-over-year. For the full fiscal year, North America organic net sales were effectively flat, representing a meaningful improvement from prior years. Our yogurt business remained a standout performer. The Greek Gods delivered strong double-digit growth along with share gains and remains an excellent example of how innovation, brand investment, and disciplined commercial execution can drive sustained results.

We are seeing emerging strength across the rest of our core business, including Celestial Seasonings Tea, which delivered growth in both the quarter and the year, driven in part by the success of our wellness tea innovation. Earth's Best Finger Foods, the largest piece of our Earth's Best business, with strong double-digit growth supported by the continued success of our self-feeding platform. More broadly, the quarter reinforced our confidence in the potential of our go-forward North American portfolio. Within our International segment, while organic net sales for Q4 declined 4% year-over-year, the decline moderated sequentially by roughly 400 basis points relative to the third quarter trends. We saw improved performance sequentially across meal prep, beverages, and baby and kids.

While spreads and drizzles remains a challenge category, we are encouraged by the early response to our Hartley's renovation and innovation launched in the fourth quarter. Combined with the improvements we are seeing across the broader portfolio, the International business is positioned well for its new ownership. We were also pleased with the improvement in profit margins delivered during the quarter. Gross margin and adjusted EBITDA margin both expanded year-over-year, driven by improvement in North America. As expected, following the Snacks divestiture, North America delivered significant improvement in profitability, reinforcing our confidence in the earnings power of the underlying portfolio and the benefits of a more focused business model.

Consistent with trends throughout fiscal 2026, the vast majority of the year's gross margin and adjusted EBITDA pressure remain concentrated within International, where inflation, productivity shortfalls, and unfavorable mix continued to weigh on profitability. More broadly, fiscal 2026 demonstrated that the actions we have taken are producing early tangible results. Exiting 2026, we see indications that the business is stabilizing, profit margins are improving, and we have a stronger operating foundation. As we enter fiscal 2027, our focus is on building on the progress made over the past year while completing the work required to establish a focused, appropriately scaled North American Hain.

Following the completion of the International transaction, our portfolio would be concentrated on leading better-for-you brands in attractive categories, including The Greek Gods yogurt, Celestial Seasonings tea, and Earth's Best finger foods and cereal. Completion of the International transaction would be an important milestone, but it would not be the end of our work. Our priorities for fiscal 2027 are clear and supported by detailed plans already underway. First, we will aggressively align our organization and cost structure with the scale and needs of the future North American business. This summer, we completed a rigorous bottoms-up, zero-based budgeting review across the organization. That work identified specific actions to align cost structure with the size of our go-forward North American business.

These actions are expected to simplify our operating model and deliver more than $16 million of annual run rate cost improvement. In addition, this exercise identified opportunities to optimize our marketing budget, driving greater impact for our key growth brands. Importantly, we expect to increase marketing investment year-over-year on both an absolute basis as well as percentage of net sales. These actions, the majority of which are expected to be implemented in fiscal 2027, support a pro forma gross margin of approximately 30-plus percent and adjusted EBITDA margin of low double-digit percentage. We have clear ownership, timing, and implementation plans and are moving with urgency to deliver these savings.

Second, we will remain disciplined in managing our financial position in light of the upcoming maturity date on the company's credit facilities in December. Proceeds from the International transaction will be used to reduce debt while maintaining rigorous oversight of working capital spending, and transformation investments. Fiscal 2027 will include investments required to execute our cost reduction program and establish the appropriate operating model for the future business. We will balance these near-term requirements with disciplined capital allocation and our continued focus on exploring any and all opportunities to further reduce debt and address the upcoming maturity. Third, we will shift investment behind our strongest brands and growth platforms.

As I just outlined, we have identified opportunities to optimize our marketing spend, and we plan to increase marketing investment year-over-year by approximately 100 basis points of net sales to support brand building and innovation across Celestial Seasonings, The Greek Gods and Earth's Best. This investment will build on the progress we are already seeing across the core portfolio. The work ahead is about establishing the right cost structure, the right portfolio, and the right level of investment to support a stronger North American Hain while continuing to explore all opportunities to maximize the value of the enterprise for the benefit of stakeholders.

The actions taken throughout fiscal 2026, together with the detailed plans underway for fiscal 2027, would position us to become a more focused, profitable, and operationally stronger company. With that, I will turn the call over to Lee to review our financial results and cost structure initiatives in even greater detail.

Lee Boyce: Thank you, Alison, and good morning, everyone. Before discussing our fourth quarter results, I would like to begin with the improvement in free cash flow and the significant reduction in debt, which were among the most important accomplishments of fiscal 2026. As Alison mentioned, we had strong cash flow delivery in the quarter. Free cash flow for the fourth quarter was $7 million, an increase compared to the outflow of $9 million in the year ago period. The improvement was primarily driven by favorable working capital performance, including benefits from accounts payable, inventory reduction, and a lower net loss, partially offset by lower accounts receivable inflow.

Free cash flow for the full year was $58 million as compared to an outflow of $3 million in the prior year. We are pleased with the progress we made on inventory driven by improved operating discipline. Days inventory outstanding improved year-over-year to 80 days in the quarter from 88 days in the prior year period. It was up compared to 73 days in Q3 2026. Note that every day of inventory is worth approximately $3 million. We made sequential progress on our days payable outstanding, with days payable outstanding of 62 days in the quarter, an improvement from 59 days in Q3 2026, but slightly below 65 days in the year ago period.

CapEx of $5 million in the quarter was down from $6 million in the prior year period. Looking ahead, we would expect capital expenditures to decrease year-over-year as our North American business is significantly less capital intensive than our international business. Strong cash flow generation this quarter brought cash on hand to $58 million and net debt to $500 million, a reduction of $151 million, or approximately 25% since the beginning of the fiscal year. We also have $186 million of available liquidity under our revolver and remain in compliance with all credit agreement covenants. With net leverage of 4.5x in the quarter, we have plenty of headroom under our covenant at 5.5x.

We have a disciplined and prudent approach to capital management and continue to prioritize debt reduction. We have reduced net debt by $277 million over the past 12 quarters. We remain in active discussions with our lenders regarding an amendment of our credit agreement to extend the current maturity date. If reached, extension would be a near-term solution and an important step that provides additional flexibility as we continue to work on reducing our leverage. We are working closely with all parties and will provide an update when we are able. We have made significant progress in the elimination of stranded costs resulting from the sale of the North American snacks business.

In fiscal 2026, we initiated actions to remove the entirety of the $25 million in stranded costs, which was ahead of our initial timeline. Additionally, our Transition Services Agreement, or TSA, is generating proceeds from providing ongoing support to the divested snacks business. Together with the actions taken to date, this has essentially eliminated any near-term stranded cost impacts. As Alison mentioned, this summer, we completed a robust bottom-up, zero-based budgeting review across the organization that identified specific actions to align cost structure with the size of our go-forward North America business. We have concrete action plans in place to enact $16 million of annual run rate cost improvement.

We expect the vast majority of that savings capture to be completed by the end of fiscal 2027, with the full completion within 18 months. We estimate the one-time cost to implement these savings will be approximately $20 million, with 70% of that incurred in fiscal 2027, and the remainder incurred in fiscal 2028. These actions will simplify our operating model and support the future growth of our North American business, implying pro forma gross margin of approximately 30%+ and low double-digit percentage adjusted EBITDA margin. Turning now to performance. For the fourth quarter, we saw an organic net sales decline of 2% year-over-year as lower sales in the international segment offset organic net sales growth in North America.

The decline in organic net sales reflected a two percentage point decrease in volume mix and flat price. Adjusted gross margin was 22.7% in the fourth quarter. This represents a 230 basis point increase year-over-year. The year-over-year increase was driven primarily by volume mix and productivity savings, partially offset by cost inflation. Additionally, there was a $1.9 million positive impact from tariff refunds in the quarter. SG&A decreased 7% year-over-year to $63 million in the fourth quarter, primarily driven by a reduction in employee-related expenses. SG&A represented 23.8% of net sales for the quarter as compared to 18.6% in the year ago period.

The increase in SG&A as a percentage of net sales was primarily driven by costs associated with the strategic review and the lower sales base. We delivered adjusted EBITDA of $19 million in the fourth quarter compared to $20 million a year ago. The decrease was driven primarily by cost inflation and a decrease in volume mix, partially offset by lower SG&A and productivity savings. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 7.1%, a 160 basis points increase from the prior year period. Interest expense fell 7% year-over-year to $12 million in the quarter, primarily driven by lower outstanding borrowings. We have hedged our rate exposure on more than 70% of our loan facility with fixed rates at 7.1%.

We continue to prioritize reducing net debt over time. Adjusted net loss, which excludes the effect of restructuring charges amongst other items, was $4 million in the quarter, or $0.05 per diluted share, as compared to adjusted net loss of $2 million or $0.02 per diluted share in the prior year period. Turning now to our individual reporting segments. In North America, organic net sales growth of 2% year-over-year was primarily driven by growth in meal prep due to strength in yogurt, partially offset by lower sales in baby and kids. Fourth quarter adjusted gross margin in North America was 31.1%, an increase of nearly 1,200 basis points versus the prior year period.

The increase was driven primarily by an increase in volume mix following the divestiture of the snacks business, as well as productivity savings, partially offset by cost inflation. Again, there was a $1.9 million positive impact from tariff refunds. Adjusted EBITDA in North America was $16 million, reflecting an increase of 55% from the year ago period and representing 14.4% of net sales. The increase resulted primarily from the reduction in SG&A as well as productivity savings, partially offset by lower volume mix and cost inflation.

In our international business, organic net sales declined 4% year-over-year in the quarter, an improvement from the 8% decline year-over-year in the third quarter, driven by sequential improvement in baby and kids, beverages, and meal prep. The year-over-year decline was primarily driven by lower sales in meal prep and baby and kids, partially offset by growth in beverages. International adjusted gross margin was 16.6%, a 555 basis points decrease versus the prior year period. The decrease was driven primarily by cost inflation, partially offset by productivity savings. Adjusted EBITDA was $12 million, reflecting a decrease of 41% compared to the prior year period and representing 8.1% of net sales.

The decrease was driven primarily by cost inflation and lower volume mix, partially offset by productivity savings. Now turning to category performance. In baby and kids, organic net sales were down 11% year-over-year, driven primarily by formula and purees in North America and purees in the U.K., partially offset by growth in finger foods in North America. We have simplified our portfolio of Earth's Best purees and are seeing a 30% increase in base velocity as a result of these strategic winning portfolio actions. Formula remains a small piece of our Earth's Best brand, where we are implementing strategic actions with a focused set of customers.

We continue to prioritize Earth's Best investment behind our key growth platforms, finger foods and cereal. In international, we are seeing improvement in Ella's Kitchen as we lap last year's industry-wide declines. In the beverages category, organic net sales were down 2% year-over-year, as 3% organic net sales growth in both tea in North America and private label non-dairy beverage in international was more than offset by the lack of promotional activity in North America. Wellness teas remained strong, growing dollar sales up high single digits and gaining share. In meal prep, organic net sales growth was 3% year-over-year. The increase was driven primarily by yogurt in North America.

The Greek Gods continue to outpace the category, growing dollar sales by high teens percent and gaining share. As a reminder, following the sales of the North American snacks business, the snacks category is comprised solely of jellies in the international segment. Organic net sales growth in snacks was down 7% year-over-year, driven by SKU rationalization as we prepare for the brand relaunch. Turning now to our outlook. As mentioned earlier, subject to the satisfaction of the closing conditions outlined in our SEC filings, we would expect the international divestiture to close in our fiscal second quarter. Net proceeds from the transaction are expected to range between $305 million and $310 million.

With these proceeds, we will pay down the entirety of our outstanding term loan and more than 35% of the outstanding balance of our revolver. Our pro forma total debt outstanding as of June 30th, 2026, would be approximately $250 million, a reduction of approximately 55%. Again, these numbers are based on the current Forex rates and are subject to change relative to Forex rates at the time of the transaction close. We remain in active discussions with our lenders to reach an agreement on the amendment of the company's credit agreement to extend the current maturity. The international divestiture is contingent upon the company securing this amendment, and there can be no assurance that an amendment will be obtained.

If the amendment is not obtained within 30 days of signing, Aurelius would have the right to terminate the agreement. We will provide updates on both the international divestiture and the credit agreement amendment as we are able. As we begin fiscal 2027, our top priority is managing our capital structure and debt while continuing to align our North American business for growth. Throughout the year, we expect that there will be various one-time costs associated with the execution of our plans. I will provide regular updates on our quarterly calls to showcase our progress. We are actively pursuing multiple components of our strategic review process that make providing traditional guidance challenging.

I look forward to sharing more on future calls. Now I turn the call back to Alison for some closing remarks.

Alison Lewis: Thanks, Lee. In closing, fiscal 2026 was a defining year for Hain. We made meaningful progress in simplifying the portfolio, paying down debt, improving cash generation, and sharpening our strategic focus on areas where we believe we can create the most value. While our transformation is not complete, we are entering fiscal 2027 as a more focused company with a stronger operational foundation and a clear plan for the work ahead. We are encouraged by the early operational progress and the improved execution across the business demonstrated in the quarter and plan on continuing to work to strengthen Hain's financial position and create value for all stakeholders.

Our priorities are straightforward: manage our capital structure and balance sheet, align our cost structure with our future North America business, continue improving operational performance, and unlock the full potential of a focused North America Hain. Given the ongoing discussions with lenders and the pending international sale, we will not be hosting a Q&A session this quarter. The update we provided on today's call and in our SEC filings is the extent of the detail that we are able to share publicly. We will provide relevant updates on the transaction and the strategic review as we are able. Finally, I want to thank our employees, customers, consumers, and other stakeholders for their continued support throughout this transformative year.

Thank you again, and I appreciate all of you joining today.

Operator: This concludes today's call. Thank you for attending. You may now disconnect.

#3085. Forget Palantir? This IPO Candidate May Be the New "Autonomy Giant" in Defense.

Shield AI nearly quadrupled in value over the past year -- and it hasn't even IPO'd yet.

If you follow defense stocks -- and artificial intelligence (AI) -- you probably know about Palantir Technologies (PLTR +5.50%). Privately owned for years before its September 2020 IPO, Palantir attracted significant investor interest even before it went public. Since Palantir went public, the stock is up 16-fold over barely six years, enough to make many investors into millionaires all on its own.

So what are the chances lightning like that could strike twice?

The chances may be better than you think, and amazing as it may sound, there's even a chance it may strike the very same kind of company: a popular defense stock focused on AI called Shield AI.

Much as Palantir was, Shield AI is a company that few people have heard of -- but it's been getting quite a lot of coverage lately and attracting the attention of defense investors. Just last week, defense news site Tectonic reported that Shield AI is raising $2.5 billion in cash at a $28.8 billion valuation to help pay for the acquisition of radar specialist Echodyne.

To put those numbers in context, Tectonic points out that as recently as March, Shield AI was valued at only $12.7 billion. So the valuation has doubled in the last eight months. What's more, as recently as 2025, Shield AI was worth only $5.3 billion. So in fact, the valuation has doubled twice in just the past year.

What is this defense contracting wunderkind? Well, according to its own website, Shield is a defense tech company with the ambitious goal of using AI-powered autonomy to guide "every military asset: aircraft, drones, ships, satellites, and submarines" by 2030.

Shield calls its own autonomy solution by the totally-not-terrifying name Hivemind -- it's the brain behind the company's V-Bat unmanned aerial vehicle (drone), its X-Bat vertical takeoff and landing fighter jet, and its Aechelon simulation platform for training both drone pilots and drone flight systems. (Aechelon also, incidentally, permits Shield's drones to operate without guidance from global positioning systems.)

As recently as a couple of months ago, I was writing about how Shield's software had become so capable that defense heavyweight L3Harris (LHX +4.44%) was enlisting its help in improving the performance of L3's VAMPIRE counter-drone rocket systems. Just one month later, Shield signed up another defense leader -- Italy's Leonardo -- to use Hivemind to power its Hivemind Proteus helicopter drone.

Elsewhere in the military, the U.S. Air Force has put Shield AI on its short list of candidates to provide autonomy software for its new fleet of Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) drone warplanes.

Clearly, Shield AI is a company on the move. Tectonic calls it the new "autonomy giant." It is also, apparently, contemplating an IPO. As Tectonic reports, Shield management is coy about its timetable, but confirms that it is definitely interested in "having the option to go public should we choose to."

Company co-founder Brandon Tseng says Shield AI is on course for $540 million in revenue this year, "up more than 80%" from 2025, according to Fortune magazine. Revenue is growing nearly as fast as the company's valuation. What's more, Tseng confirms that "we don't expect growth to slow down."

So what does this imply for Shield AI's valuation? Well, $540 million in revenue on a stock with a $28.8 billion valuation means Shield stock is valued at approximately 53 times sales. That's actually a bit less than what Palantir stock costs (61 times sales), despite Shield being earlier in its growth trajectory and having more room to grow.

Granted, Palantir's a much bigger player in this market. Its $7.3 billion in trailing revenue still dwarfs Shield's $540 million. But with the momentum Shield is showing, that may not remain the case for long. In a growing military market that's clearly very interested in autonomy, Shield AI could prove a popular choice -- for the Pentagon and for IPO investors.

Rich Smith has no position in any of the stocks mentioned. The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends L3Harris Technologies and Palantir Technologies. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy.

#3084. $6.3 billion Binance hack is largest crypto theft on record

Binance said Friday that a security incident impacted about $6.3 billion in client assets, with around $3 billion frozen on-chain, marking the largest crypto hack on record.

The company later added it began recovering assets impacted by the breach after pledging to cover losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users, which the company created in 2018 as a protection for clients in the event of a hack.

It wasn't clear how the attack took place. The world's largest crypto exchange initially said the hack may involve "a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." However, Co-CEO Richard Teng later said the attack involved a more complex process rather than the misuse of a single engineer's permissions.

The FBI said Friday it was aware of the incident and was in touch with "relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity, evaluate ​potential impacts, ​and ⁠coordinate appropriate investigative steps."

It wasn't clear either who was responsible for the breach. But TRM Labs, a blockchain intelligence and AI investigations company, pointed to North Korean hackers as the potential culprits. "Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists, including the Bybit hack and the KelpDAO hack in April 2026: small Tornado Cash withdrawals funding an operator wallet, staging that began well before the theft, and signatures obtained in advance then executed in one burst," the company said in a post.

Blockchain data platform Chainalysis also said this appears "be the work of North Korean cybercrime group TraderTraitor. This group has repeatedly targeted the cryptocurrency industry, exchanges, DeFi protocols, and investors, to raise funds for the regime. We base our intelligence assessment on on-chain activity observed in the hours following the hack."

Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals while it overhauls its withdrawal security systems and has revoked the affected address authorizations, Teng said. The exchange is also working with law enforcement and blockchain intelligence firms to trace and recover the stolen funds, while deposits remain unaffected.

Binance co-founder Yi He said deposits remained unaffected and continued to operate normally, while the exchange was working on enhancements to its withdrawal service and related address controls. It expects to begin resuming withdrawal services within the next 48 hours.

"We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are fully verified," Binance said.

The announcement followed moves by several crypto firms, including Circle Internet Group, Tether and Ripple, to freeze funds tied to the hack.

Exploits are not uncommon in the crypto space. In 2025, Bybit suffered roughly $1.5 billion in losses due to a hack. More recently, Bitget lost more than $350 million worth of digital assets in a cyber theft incident. Over the past several years, bad actors have also drained billions of dollars in crypto from decentralized exchanges.

This week's breach "proves our exact point in proposing regulations for crypto markets earlier this month," Michael Selig, chairman of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, said Friday in a CNBC "Squawk on the Street" interview. The U.S. derivatives regulator on Oct. 5 proposed a framework that would effectively put crypto exchanges under federal government oversight — after Congress failed to approve legislation to regulate the asset.

"The real issue here is that these are unregulated offshore exchanges, and they don't have the same sorts of safeguards that we have in our financial markets here in the United States. We want to offer a federal option to these exchanges to come and register with the CFTC, and they would be subject to the same sorts of cyber security safeguards that we have in our markets today," he said.

Bitcoin fell more than 4% to $77,187.60 on Friday as the hack weighed on crypto markets.

Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said Thursday evening in a social media post that the company had frozen more than 800 million in USD Coin associated with the incident. USDT stablecoin issuer Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino also said in on X that his firm had frozen more than 1.5 billion of its stablecoin that may have been related to a potential breach.

Jack McDonald, Ripple's senior vice president of stablecoins, said it was actively freezing affected funds held in RLUSD, its U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin.

#3083. Best Hotels in Chase’s The Edit in 2026

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site or when you click to or take an action on their website. This compensation helps us provide tools and services - like free credit score access and monitoring. With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

Chase's hotel and resort program, The Edit, gives some cardholders the chance to book stays at spectacular hotels.

Many premium credit cards have their own travel portals where you can earn and redeem your points. They also have a curated list of hotels with which they partner to offer elevated benefits to their cardholders who book directly through their program.

The Edit is Chase’s program, and similar to the Fine Hotels & Resorts program from American Express, travelers need to book a prepaid reservation directly through a Chase Travel channel and pay with their Chase card to receive the benefits.

What benefits do you receive when you book through the program? Well, they can be substantial.

At nearly 1,400 hotels and resorts, The Edit customers will enjoy:

If the hotel is an all-inclusive property, guests would instead receive a $200 property credit to use for experiences like spa treatments. While stays at hotels in The Edit Boutique Collection do include the other perks, those stays are not eligible for a room upgrade or early check-in/late checkout considerations.

The tradeoff of using The Edit program is that it does not necessarily always have the lowest rate. Sometimes you can find a lower rate directly with the hotel or another website. But, when you consider the list of benefits above, any differential in price can more than outweigh the extra cost.

While it belongs to Chase, The Edit is not open to all Chase cardholders. It is a dedicated perk for primary cardholders and authorized users of the Chase Sapphire Reserve® and J.P. Morgan Reserve cards, as well as primary Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ cardholders.

Even better is that these eligible Chase cards come with a total of $500 in credits that can be used at The Edit hotels each year. They are divided into two $250 credits that each must be used for at least a two-night stay. And when paying for the rest of your stay through The Edit, cardholders earn 8x Chase Ultimate Rewards® points per dollar spent. In addition, hotel stays booked through The Edit and labeled as “Loyalty Plus” are eligible to also earn points with any associated hotel loyalty program.

These are some of our favorite hotels in the program where you can take advantage of your annual $500 credits as well as earn significant Chase points for a prepaid stay.

This oasis in the desert enjoys distant views of the Atlas Mountains from its various pools and riad-like accommodation buildings. It also has a full-service spa, kids club and access to Al Maaden Golf course. Its Moroccan restaurant is worth a visit and offers cuisine from all of Morocco and the North African region (with many ingredients coming from the chef’s onsite garden). Guests can add a stash of World of Hyatt points to their account after a stay here, but be sure to look to see if it is “eligible” in the search results (as shown below).

Guests can arrive at this luxury resort by its own fleet of two sea planes that serve the three properties in the Four Seasons portfolio. (Two of the properties are in The Edit, the third is a private island: Four Seasons Maldives Kuda Huraa, Four Seasons Resort Maldives at Landaa Giraavaru and Four Seasons Maldives Private Island at Voavah, respectively.)

Overwater villas with their own pools and hammocks dangling over the sea, beach bungalows with private access pools and excellent dining (from Asian to Lebanese) are hallmarks of the resort. Its newest element is the AyurMa wellness program at the spa with onsite practitioners who guide guests on personalized, multiday journeys covering everything from nutrition to physical therapy.

This resort is designed around 64 pool suites and villas with access to a beautiful beachfront, swimming pools and a jungle spa. Its island location lies within the Gulf of Thailand near Koh Samui, and its beach is well-known for its famous Full Moon parties. Other activities, besides relaxing, include Muay Thai boxing, scuba diving, snorkeling, kayaking, stand-up paddle boarding and yoga sessions.

Anantara is part of Minor Hotels that are associated with the Discovery program, which means travelers can earn Discovery Dollars, even when booking via The Edit.

Along the Southbank Promenade, this luxury hotel has great views of the Melbourne skyline and is within walking distance of the city’s great shopping, museums and dining options. When you enter the lobby, the first thing you notice is the grand Waterford crystal chandelier, one of the largest in the Southern Hemisphere.

This is also one of the city’s biggest hotels, and it is highly regarded as a top hotel in town. Be sure to request one of the rooms with a balcony or terrace to take in the views.

Known by many as Dublin’s grande dame, this Autograph Collection member is fresh off the heels of a top-to-bottom renovation that renewed its interiors, but didn’t change its historic spirit. While renovation work will linger into 2027, the refreshed rooms are worth experiencing.

The hotel is where the drafting of the Irish Constitution took place, but today it serves as a hub for visiting elite and locals to mix and mingle. When booking through The Edit, members can earn Marriott Bonvoy points in addition to Chase Ultimate Rewards®.

This beachfront hotel is a favorite destination for European travelers who want a Dalmatian coastline view while also being in close proximity to the historic center of town. There are multiple pools, a beach club and spa for onsite entertainment. Radisson Rewards members would also be able to earn points for their stay.

Radisson is growing its portfolio of high-end hotels, resorts and luxury properties, which makes the loyalty program one not to overlook for Americans who may not be as familiar with it.

This city-center hotel is ideal for business travelers, but also attracts attention for its rooftop bar and restaurant. Chase cardholders using The Edit should think beyond just booking a vacation stay through the program because business trips can also yield significant Ultimate Rewards points bonuses. Just remember you need to book through The Edit with a prepaid, eligible rate.

In a historic bank building, the hotel’s Bauhaus-inspired design with colorful art make this more than just a standard business property. And like Kimpton properties worldwide, guests here can take advantage of morning coffee and refreshments in the lobby, an evening happy hour, free bikes and yoga mats to use, and of course the secret password. Mention that password (which changes seasonally) at reception to be eligible for a prize that could include drink vouchers or room upgrades among other things.

This family-friendly resort features the largest and first waterpark on the island (with three waterslides and a lazy river) as well as some of its finest dining venues, including the only high-end steakhouse on the island. Golfers can enjoy the island’s only 18-hole golf course here, too.

Because it's an independent resort, booking through The Edit is a great way to still earn points for your stay since it does not have a loyalty program of its own.

Celebrating 100 years, the hotel has unveiled renovations across the hotel, which sits in midtown Manhattan, and they will continue for the next year. Guests who book a Club rate or have the annual lounge benefit they can select as a Milestone Reward can visit the lobby-level club lounge here.

The building was built as part of the Grand Central Terminal design plan and now belongs to the Historic Hotels of America group. Guests who book through The Edit will receive IHG One Rewards for their stay and any eligible elite status perks.

The “Pink Palace of the Pacific” will celebrate its 100th anniversary in 2027 and is a famous hotel along one of Hawaii’s most famous beaches. This is one of many Marriott Bonvoy family hotels in Honolulu, and it is surrounded by lush gardens and has stunning ocean views. Guests can walk to nearby shopping, take the onsite history tour or snap photos with Diamond Head in the background. Guests can earn Marriott Bonvoy points for their stay, and elite status members can take advantage of any eligible perks.

This all-inclusive, family hotel is a great option for those looking for great dining, sunshine and oceanfront accommodations. Parents can enjoy the spa while kids are having fun in the kids club. Other activities include movie nights outside, painting classes, beach barbecues and lawn games. The resort is part of the Preferred Hotels & Resorts program, and earning Ultimate Rewards points for booking a stay through The Edit is a nice bonus.

Prepare for a new experience at one of the Chilean capital’s most posh hotels, and you can book your entire stay through The Edit. As a result, you would receive the perks of the program as well as Marriott Bonvoy points at the only Ritz-Carlton in South America.

Big changes at the hotel include new menus that refocus the restaurant cuisine on modern takes of Chilean recipes. The chef partners with a local farmer for produce, but goes one step further in being able to have first dibs on the best produce and herbs available each season. On the top floor, guests can enjoy a panoramic indoor swimming pool beneath a glass atrium, panoramic rooftop terrace and spa offering traditional Andean healing treatments.

Booking a hotel via The Edit leads to instant benefits like free breakfast, property credits, and early check-in and late checkout. While the rates may not always be the lowest you’ll find online, the perks that come with The Edit may more than outweigh any cost differential.

The Edit’s curated collection of hotels and resorts covers a broad range of high-end properties, and the program is only open to select Chase credit cardholders. When making a prepaid, eligible reservation through The Edit, the cardholder also receives 8x Ultimate Rewards points on top of the onsite perks that make this a great offer. Even better, if the property participates in its own loyalty program, Chase has worked out that members can double dip and earn Chase Ultimate Rewards® and the relevant hotel points and potential elite status perks, too (as long as it is labeled as “eligible” in the search function).

Don’t forget about the $500 in built-in credits that come with your card, which renew each year and only further the value with Chase’s The Edit program.

#3081. Axon Enterprise: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Axon's $15.8 billion in future contracted bookings gives the company a multi-year runway, but its inventory buildup is already weighing on free cash flow.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 5, 2026, Axon (AXON -3.14%) announced an expanded partnership and a $1.2 billion investment in autonomous drone maker Skydio. For long-term shareholders, the moves reveal how the public safety technology maker plans to capture airspace intelligence while managing shifting federal hardware timelines. Three things management said stand out.

Management put $1.2 billion behind autonomous aerial technology to secure exclusive public safety distribution rights in the U.S. and Canada. Building out hardware supply chains requires substantial capital, so taking a 37% equity stake lets Skydio fund its development while Axon integrates flying hardware directly into its software ecosystem.

Complex federal counter-drone deployments involve extended procurement processes and site preparation. Because these large hardware shipments create quarterly revenue volatility, management reset its forecasting practice to include federal deals in official guidance only after shipments are fully confirmed.

Management added over $100 million in inventory during the third quarter to shield operations from potential component shortages. Carrying extra inventory reduces near-term free cash flow conversion, but the company's core hardware avoids obsolescence risk and protects customer trust.

High-margin software revenue is expanding across real-time operational platforms, while management focuses on monetizing its multiyear contracted backlog. The company maintains durable moat protection through deep customer relationships, proprietary body sensors, and connected software workflows. Strategic priorities center on operational leverage and disciplined inventory control.

As public safety agencies deploy artificial intelligence and connected hardware, maintaining agency trust is essential to long-term market leadership.
