VA mortgage borrowers are quietly navigating a knowledge gap. Here’s how to close it.

If your understanding of a VA home loan starts and ends with “it’s for the military,” you’re not alone. For many eligible veterans and service members, the intricate workings (and benefits) of this U.S. government-backed mortgage are obscured behind lackluster guidance.

While there are classes and resources available, the military is broadly wary of steering members in a specific direction, says Alex Rodino, a real estate agent and U.S. Army veteran who served 10 years as an infantry officer and military advisor. “A lot of the course material is just very generic,” he says.

And that’s not a surprise. Considering the sheer size and scope of the military, providing personalized advice on VA loans to all its members would be no easy task.

That leaves real estate agents and lenders as the last line of defense, which is where a big part of the knowledge gap exists. Rodino purchased his first home in 2020 with a VA loan and says he didn’t like how ignorant he felt during the process.

“The reason I actually got my real estate license to begin with was because of that experience I had,” Rodino says. “Looking back on it, I had a lot of questions that didn't really get answered.”

But how can VA borrowers navigate this knowledge gap without having to become mortgage experts in their spare time? Here are some of the most important things to know when considering a VA loan, according to the financial experts and borrowers who have lived it.

“My mortgage broker said, hey, you might qualify for this, look it up,” says Elizabeth Valente, a real estate investor and former U.S. Army officer who bought her first home using a VA loan in 2021. When it came to the application process, she felt crucial information wasn’t readily available to her or fully explained.

In hindsight, Valente says, working with an agent or lender who had detailed VA loan experience would have been beneficial. Not only would it help untangle the specific paperwork and appraisal requirements, but that expertise offers an important layer of support for military borrowers.

“For some processes in the military, it's very hand-holding,” Valente says. “I'll tell you what to wear, what to bring, when to be there.” But that’s not always true when transitioning back to civilian life, and parsing specifics of a loan process can be challenging. “I don't think a typical Realtor would understand what that person's going through,” Valente says.

Finding professionals with the right expertise involves asking questions — and lots of them.

“If I'm the smartest person in the room, we have an issue,” Valente says. “Don't be afraid to tell someone if something doesn't make sense or if you don't understand the numbers.”

Before agreeing to work with a lender or mortgage broker, ask how their process works, what companies they work with, and how familiar they are with VA loans. Treat the initial conversation like an interview — you’re hiring them, not the other way around.

Knowing where to find your Certificate of Eligibility (COE) and how much you might be eligible to borrow is the responsibility of the person applying, Valente says. “All that information — it is available in the [VA] website but you really have to dig for it.”

And this information isn’t recreational reading — your COE lists your "basic entitlement," which is a crucial figure in VA lending. If you have full basic entitlement, the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) generally guarantees 25% of the loan, which in most cases lets you put 0% down.

Why? With a quarter of the loan guaranteed by the VA, the lender is more protected and thus more willing to forgo a down payment.

So how do you know if you have full basic entitlement? Look for the figure $36,000 on your COE. This dollar amount represents full entitlement. Technically, basic entitlement is for loans up to $144,000, but then your bonus entitlement kicks in and you can go higher. The VA doesn’t set loan limits when you have full entitlement — though your lender will still decide how much you can borrow based on your income, debts, credit and the home’s appraised value.

Let’s say you want to buy a home in Fayetteville, North Carolina, and you need a $200,000 loan. In order to put no money down, your entitlement needs to cover at least 25% of the loan amount — in this example, that’s $50,000. After you purchase the home, your COE will show your basic entitlement as $0 and the entitlement charged to a previous loan as $50,000.

“Serving in the military is a unique investing opportunity that most people don't get,” Rodino says. “I wish someone had told me to buy a house when I got to my first duty station.”

If he’d known it was possible or understood how, Rodino says he would have been able to buy in 2017, move in 2020, rent out his first home and then repeat the process. “I'd have three by now and the first one would probably be paid off.”

This particular plan is partly based on the unique schedule of many military members. “Generally, you're moving anywhere from two to four to six years,” Rodino says. Owning multiple properties also leverages two big (and often misunderstood) perks of the VA loan: It’s possible to have more than one active loan at the same time, and after one year, you may be able to convert your primary residence to a rental.

Let’s go back to Fayetteville, North Carolina. After two years, you decide to rent out the home because you’re moving to Bell County, Texas. The home you want to buy in Bell County is $300,000, and in order to make no down payment, you need the VA to guarantee 25% of the loan ($75,000).

Because you no longer have full basic entitlement — remember, you already have an active VA loan elsewhere — your entitlement is capped at 25% of the conforming loan limit in the county where you plan to buy, minus what’s already being used on your first loan ($50,000 in our Fayetteville example).

Now for the math: The current conforming loan limit in Bell County is $832,750. Multiply this figure by 25% and subtract the $50,000 already in use: You have $158,187.50 of entitlement available to you — plenty to guarantee the $75,000 needed on the new loan.

If all of this sounds overwhelming, you’re not wrong. There are resources out there to help you figure all of this out, Rodino says. “The problem is, they're not always practical or they're not always apparent.”

The VA has a website that can walk you through entitlement calculations, but you should also ask your lender, broker or agent. If you’re working with experienced folks, they’ll be able to explain these details and help you get the most out of the VA’s guarantees.

The key takeaway is this: While each VA loan must initially be for a primary residence, borrowers can leverage their entitlement to build an investment portfolio without needing to cough up large down payments.

But these examples don’t consider all of the factors that go into approvals. Like most mortgages, your income, debts and assets dictate your eligibility. And although the VA doesn’t impose credit score minimums, most lenders do — NerdWallet's analysis shows 620 is a common floor.

It’s also important to note that a VA loan’s 0% down isn’t free. VA loans carry a funding fee based on how much you’re putting down and whether it’s your first or subsequent use (certain disabled veterans are exempt). You can pay this up front at closing or roll it into the loan amount; again, your team of professionals should be able to walk you through your options.

“I think there's the assumption that this is what we do: We get our VA home loan and we go buy a home,” says Julie Soares, financial readiness director for the Wounded Warrior Project. When we’re given access to a benefit that offers discounts and perks, it can be hard not to take advantage of it. But this is why financial awareness is critical.

There are a lot of conversations happening right now around homeownership and whether it’s the right choice, especially as affordability remains challenging. So if you haven’t heard it recently, here’s a reminder: Buying property is not the only way to build wealth or create financial security.

“The financial readiness program at Wounded Warrior Project is really leaning into getting further upstream in those conversations,” Soares says. Having a clear understanding of your benefits before you need to use them allows you to make more informed choices.

While it's helpful to understand your entitlement and what you may be eligible to borrow, you don't have to know every little detail about mortgages, or navigate the process alone. Sometimes, the most important thing to know about VA loans is where to turn for help.

If you are unsure of your eligibility or want more information about home loans, you can call the VA's home loans hotline at 877-827-3702.

“Please reach out to Wounded Warrior Project, reach out to the VA, reach out to any service organization,” Soares says. “Not one organization is gonna be able to fix or solve all of these problems. We have to do this as a group.”

#3076. TransMedics: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Its ENHANCE heart and DENOVO lung programs target thousands of procedures that currently use no machine preservation at all.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 5, 2026, TransMedics (TMDX +6.29%) announced full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $764 million to $774 million. The company is advancing several clinical initiatives to expand the use of its medical devices across donor organs. Three things management said stand out for long-term investors.

Third-quarter revenue reached $203 million, up 41% year over year, despite the typical summer lull in donor activity. Increasing customer adoption of organ preservation technology helped offset a 6% drop in overall U.S. donor organ availability during the quarter.

Management is expanding enrollment in its ENHANCE heart and DENOVO lung clinical programs, which use warm perfusion and cold storage options to broaden patient eligibility. These initiatives aim to capture thousands of annual procedures that currently use no machine preservation technology.

TransMedics is developing a portable kidney system to address organs currently discarded due to prolonged ischemia or damage from lack of blood flow during transport. First human clinical testing remains scheduled for the second half of 2027.

Case volumes are reaching all-time highs as hospital adoption expands. TransMedics relies on its owned aviation fleet and donor screening services while management tracks European expansion and clinical trial progress.

Manufacturing efficiencies and next-generation organ preservation systems are expected to drive operating leverage as new clinical indications scale.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

The company has transitioned its transformation program from the implementation phase to the optimization of warehouse and route efficiencies. Like much of the industry, we have responded to higher fuel costs, with the surcharge across our customer base. it is a partial recovery by design, and we will continue to manage it actively as diesel prices move so that it helps offset fuel cost over time while keeping our pricing competitive.

Adjusted EBITDA decreased 6.3% to $11 million for the quarter compared to $11.7 million in the prior year quarter. And included $600 thousand from 1 month of contribution from Sea Ray. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 3.4% compared to 3.8% in the prior year quarter. For the first 9 months, adjusted EBITDA was $34.7 million down less than 2% from last year despite the fuel headwind. Fuel headwinds in the quarter and year to date were approximately 1.4 million and $3.2 million, respectively. Total interest expense was $3.4 million for the quarter compared to $2.9 million in the prior year quarter.

The increase reflects the higher term loan balance following our July refinancing partially offset by the mortgage debt we repaid as part of that transaction. Net loss attributable to HF Foods was a loss of $4.2 million for the quarter compared to a loss of $1.1 million in the prior year quarter. The increase of $3.1 million was primarily driven by a $2.9 million decrease in income from operations and a $900 thousand unfavorable change in income taxes partially offset by a $900 thousand favorable year-over-year change in the fair value of our interest rate swaps. Adjusted net income attributable to HF Foods was $2.1 million for the quarter compared to $4.3 million in the prior year quarter.

Loss per share was $0.08 for the quarter compared to a loss of $0.02 per share in the prior year quarter. Adjusted net income per share was $0.04 per quarter compared to $0.08 in the prior year quarter. Now on CapEx. We spent approximately $22.3 million for the 9 months ended September 30, 2026. The largest item remains the purchase of our previously leased Chicago distribution center. Which we discussed last quarter, along with investments in solar and capacity expansion. With the Chicago purchase behind us, spending slowed meaningfully in the third quarter. On the solar investment, we expect to benefit from a onetime investment tax credit that will reduce our overall solar investment by approximately 40%.

Separately, our fleet renewal is already paying off in lower repair and maintenance costs, and we expect this to continue. Turning to the balance sheet. As we discussed on last quarter's earnings call, we refinanced and upsized our credit facility in July. That gave us liquidity to close the Sea Ray acquisition while continuing to invest in our facilities. Cash for cash provided by operating activities was $23.6 million for the first 9 months of 2026. More than 5 times the $4.5 million in the prior year period driven mainly by a smaller inventory build than last year when we purchased ahead of tariff increases along with the timing of working capital.

As of September 30, 2026, after closing Sea Ray, we had cash of $16.4 million and access to approximately $49.1 million in additional funds through a $140 million line of credit subject to a borrowing base calculation. Turning to Sea Ray. We owned it for 1 month of the quarter, so this is an early read. But it is an encouraging 1. As Felix mentioned, Sea Ray's first month came in the mid teens adjusted EBITDA margin, more than 4x our consolidated margin this quarter, on a business we acquired at approximately 5x its 2025 adjusted EBITDA.

That makes Sea Ray accretive to our consolidated margin from its first month and a tailwind towards the 4.5% to 5%+ consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin target we have laid out. The fourth quarter will be our first full quarter with Sea Ray and our results. And we like what we have seen so far. Let me close by putting the quarter into a broader context. The top line and cash flow were strong, Profitability was not. We understand why. A meaningful part of this quarter's cost pressure came from onetime cost of transactions we chose to undertake and both of those transactions leave us in a stronger position.

Fuel is the piece we do not control, and we have acted on it. Underneath that, this is our seventh consecutive quarter of year over year net revenue growth for the first 9 months of 2026, net revenue is up 3.8% to $955.4 million. Sea Ray now adds a higher margin growth engine on top of that base. We head into the fourth quarter with 3 things working for us. First, the fourth quarter will be our first full quarter with Sea Ray, at a margin several times that of our total consolidated margins. Second, the fuel surcharge program is now in place. And third, the nonrecurring transaction costs that weighed in on this quarter are largely behind us.

We took on debt this year to buy our Chicago facility and Sea Ray. Both add earnings capacity and our refinancing facility gives us the runway with maturities out to 2020-2030 to grow into that leverage. We will stay disciplined on the capital deployment and selective on the tuck in opportunities that strengthen the platform. The balance sheet capacity we created is there to support that, And as noted before, Sea Ray is the first demonstration of what we intend to do with it. With that, I will turn the call back to Felix.

Xi Lin: Thanks, Paul. Before we move to Q&A, I want to come back to why Sea Ray is such a significant milestone. for us. We have talked for a long time about extending our platform beyond The United States. And Sea Ray is a first step in our long-stated strategy. Sea Ray has spent 25 years building its business in Canada. And we are proud to welcome the team to HF Foods. Just as Sea Ray gives us a platform to grow in Canada, we believe its recently established US operations, including a planned direct import operation, in Los Angeles, can be accelerated by our distribution network. Sorting scale, and West Coast infrastructure.

Sea Ray also brings a customer base that includes retail, wholesale, and restaurants. Now our focus is on executing well. Completing a smooth integration with the Sea Ray team and capturing the cross selling and supply chain synergies between our 2 businesses. Alongside that, we will keep managing through fuel cost pressure, driving efficiencies across our network. And staying disciplined as we evaluate further opportunities that strengthen the platform. Thank you for your continued support. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter. I will now turn it over to the operator for Q&A.

Operator: Thank you. We will now be conducting a question and answer session. You may press 2 if you would like to remove your question from the queue. For participants using speaker equipment, it may be necessary to pick up your handset before pressing the star keys. 1 moment, please, while we poll for questions. Our first question is from Aaron Grey with Alliance Global Partners. Please proceed with your question.

Aaron Grey: Hi, good evening, and thank you very much for the questions. First question for me, I just want to get an update in terms of where you stand on some of your cross selling initiatives. I think you mentioned last call, you know, some might be able to be starting at the end of 2026. So any update there? And then how we should think about the timing of some of the cross selling opportunities as part of the top line synergies, with the Sea Ray acquisition? Thanks.

Xi Lin: Hi, Aaron. Yes. So if you look at Q3 specifically, most of the growth have been driven by seafood volume. I think that is part of our cross selling strategy specifically in the East. In the Southeast kind of kicking in. So I would say that is still very much in the front end of it. So I think we expect in 2027, there is perhaps going to be a little bit larger cross selling piece to the growth strategy. Especially where investments are going in Chicago as well. Where we are trying to get into nonfrozen seafood business. So again, overall, we are still in the early stages of that.

When we quantify the overall cross selling opportunity, you know, several hundred million dollars of organic growth opportunity, that is really over a 3- to 5-year period. So we do expect that in the subsequent years, that number is gonna grow from here. And then from CRA standpoint, I think we are still in the very beginning phase of that. I think the focus right now is how do we integrate the business in fully from a systems and data and all that standpoint, So we expect over the next few months, that is gonna be the priority before we get into a full cross selling or synergy exploration. Okay. Great. Thanks, Xi.

Second question for me, on the Sea Ray acquisition. Right? So I kind of appreciate it is still early days of having closed it. Just maybe initial indication in terms of, you know, how it is been relative to your expectations. I know it is been a while since you had, you know, a larger acquisition. So just the team's ability to integrate it, how's that been relative, to your expectations And how that could impact how much more you could take on potentially with another acquisition as you continue to evaluate. You know, the end result is not only trying to gain efficiency through our own core business, it is also to make sure we have a ready-to-go M&A integration playbook. So I think what we are seeing especially through the first month, you know, couple months of owning Sea Ray, we are seeing that M&A playbook, you know, come in into play here. From a capacity standpoint, again, we are always going to be very optimistic. 12, 18 months ago, we talked about Sea Ray was not necessarily on the radar screen. But because we are the acquirer of choice, not only, you know, in The US market, but now we have proven the fact that we are in the Canadian market as well. So the pipeline is still very much, you know, vibrant.

We are just gonna be evaluating these as they come in. But we do expect that M&A will continue to be a core part of our growth strategy here on a go forward basis. Okay. Great. Thanks for the call. I will jump back in the queue.

And now with Sea Ray, you know, acquisition coming into play. That will have a material, you know, implication in terms of how 2027 is gonna go. Oh, I think going through the whole Sea Ray acquisition process, it certainly opened up a whole new kind of a market for us. But I think there are a lot of opportunities there. So we do see there are potential other targets that have similar financial profiles compared to Sea Ray. But, again, you know, if you look at from an M&A standpoint, there is all these different criteria that we are looking at.

So, again, we have a pretty significant pipeline and all these different targets fit into different bills of it. So I think we just gotta evaluate them as they come up and certainly, we are trying to be patient, exercise a little bit of caution. But, again, I think 2027 we do expect ourselves to be continue to be active here on the M&A front. Thank you. I appreciate all that context, Xi.

Operator: We have now reached the end of the question and answer session. I would like to turn the floor back over to Xi Lin for closing comments.

Xi Lin: Again, I want to thank everyone for paying attention and continue to support HF Foods. So we expect again, over the next several quarters, some of these. Hopefully, the factors impacting us subside. But the future still remains very bright for the company, and we look forward to continue to execute on our plan.

I look forward to updating you guys on our progress here in the next quarter. Thank you.

#3066. First Look: Inside United’s New Club at Washington Dulles

The airline’s newest lounge will be the second-largest in the network, offering flyers an upgraded experience at Dulles.

You’ll no longer have to go to the basement to get into a United Club at Washington Dulles International Airport.

The brand-new United Club in the new IAD Concourse E spans nearly 40,000 square feet across an upstairs floor and can seat 630 passengers, making it a significant upgrade to the carrier’s existing lounge portfolio at the airport. It’s the second-largest United Club after its newest lounge in Houston, which opened just weeks earlier.

The new lounge by gates E14 and E16 opens to customers Nov. 10, 2026. United invited me to a media preview of the lounge, and here’s what you can expect inside.

The lounge features several nods to D.C.’s iconic landmarks and monuments, as well as the region’s natural beauty.

When you first enter the lounge, you’ll need to scan your boarding pass and then head up the escalators (stairs and elevators are also available) to get to the lounge.

One of my favorite design features as a former D.C. resident is that escalator ride up, which has been recreated to feel like you’re inside a Metro station.

Thankfully, the escalator ride is not as long as at some stations. Looking at you, Dupont Circle!

Once you're upstairs, you’ll walk into the heart of the lounge, with two buffet stations, a centerpiece bar and plenty of seating options, whether you’re traveling as a group or by yourself. (More on food and beverage options later.)

It’s impossible to miss the soaring ceilings in this lounge, especially compared to the bunker-like atmosphere at some of the existing United Clubs.

Don’t forget to look up, where you’ll see a cherry blossom sculpture, an homage to one of the region’s most popular attractions.

There are also two additional lounging areas on both sides of the central area. One is inspired by the Blue Ridge Mountains, which you can see in the distance.

The other has a cherry blossom theme, with light fixtures that branch out from the ceiling.

Massive windows run throughout the lounge, allowing in tons of natural light and offering fantastic views of the airfield. United has a major presence at IAD, so expect to see plenty of United planes.

The United Club has a full kitchen, allowing it to offer upgraded food options compared to its existing lounges at IAD.

You can expect to find sandwiches, salads and hot protein dishes. The lounge also had a ramen bar and a chili bar set up during my visit.

The two buffet stations are located right next to each other, with a dessert station in between.

If you want something to drink, you can head to the bar or one of the hydration stations throughout the space.

There’s plenty of seating at the bar, which has a double archway design. There are also large TVs if you’re trying to keep up with one of Washington’s many sports teams.

The United Club has eight phone booths for those who need to make a call. They’re split between the two lounging areas in the club.

You'll also find a single-stall private restroom, a wellness room, and dedicated men’s and women’s restrooms.

There are no showers in this lounge. To access a shower in a United lounge, you’ll need to head to the Polaris Lounge, reserved exclusively for eligible business class passengers flying on United and select partner airlines.

You can access the United Club by holding elite status, a lounge membership, the right credit card or an eligible premium cabin ticket.

If there’s availability, United sells day passes at the door for flights departing within three hours. You’ll also need a valid same-day boarding pass on a United or Star Alliance flight.

Holding the right credit card is probably the easiest way to get in. United’s most high-end card comes with a United Club membership, while others might offer one-time passes.

If you’re looking for a United lounge, the newest club in Concourse E is where you want to be. It offers more space, lots of light and elevated food options compared to other United Clubs.

Its massive footprint could also ease overcrowding, a common complaint with other lounges.

One thing to consider is location. The concourses at IAD are spread out, and you may need to take a mobile lounge or train to get there. If you want to check out the lounge, make sure you give yourself enough time to get to your gate.

#3062. LifeVantage (LFVN) Q1 2027 Earnings Call Transcript

Sales slid 22% as management overhauls strategy and shifts its fiscal calendar.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

LifeVantage Corporation (LFVN +1.34%) reported a double-digit revenue decline for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 as management initiated a comprehensive strategic transformation. The company is shifting toward a brand-driven, consumer-focused model intended to stabilize a base of active accounts that decreased by 19% year over year. Financial priorities include resetting the cost structure and reinvesting in digital capabilities to modernize the selling proposition. To align strategy with performance cycles, the company will transition its fiscal year to match the calendar year beginning Jan. 1, 2027. Management did not provide formal financial guidance for the upcoming period but emphasized a focus on operational efficiency and the stabilization of average order sizes.

Operator: Good day, ladies and gentlemen. Thank you for standing by. Welcome to today's conference call to discuss LifeVantage's first Quarter Fiscal Year 27 Results. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. Following the formal remarks, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. Instructions will be provided at that time for you to queue up. Hosting today's conference will be Reed Anderson with ICR. As a reminder, today's conference is being recorded. And now, I would like to turn the conference over to Mr. Anderson. Please go ahead.

Reed Anderson: Thank you, and good afternoon, everyone. And welcome to LifeVantage Corporation's conference call to results for the quarter ended 09/30/2026. On the call today from LifeVantage, are Terrence O. Moorehead, President and Chief Executive Officer and Carl A. Aure, Chief Financial Officer. By now, everyone should have access to the earnings release which went out this afternoon at approximately 04:05PM Eastern Time. If you have not received this release, it is available on the Investor Relations portion of LifeVantage's website at www.lifevantage.com. This call is being webcast, and a replay will be available on the company's website as well.

Before we begin, we would like to remind everyone that our prepared remarks contain forward looking statements and management may make additional forward looking statements in response to your questions. These statements do not guarantee future performance, and therefore, undue reliance should not be placed upon them. These statements are based on the current expectations of the company's management and involve inherent risks and uncertainties, including those identified in the Risk Factors section of LifeVantage's most recently filed forms 10 ks and 10 Q. Please note that during today's call, we will discuss non GAAP financial measures including results on an adjusted basis.

Management believes these financial measures can facilitate a more complete analysis and greater transparency into LifeVantage's ongoing results of operations particularly when comparing underlying operating results from period to period. We have included reconciliation of these non-GAAP measures with today's release. This call also contains time sensitive information that is accurate only as of the date of this live broadcast 11/09/2026. LifeVantage assumes no obligation to update any forward looking projections that may be made in today's release or call. Now I will turn the call over to Terrence O. Moorehead, President and Chief Executive Officer of LifeVantage.

Terrence O. Moorehead: Thank you, Reed, and good afternoon, everyone. Today, I am going to walk you through some of the initial progress we have made and provide a brief outline of our plans moving forward. Carl is going to walk you through our first quarter performance and financials in a few minutes. But I want to use my time today to focus primarily on where we go from here. I have been with LifeVantage for just over 90 days. And during that time, I have taken the opportunity to listen, learn, and work with our consultants, consumers, employees, and board. I joined the company believing LifeVantage, had far greater potential than its current scale reflects.

And after a comprehensive review of the business, I believe that even more strongly, today. But we have a lot of work to do. In the first quarter, our sales saw revenue decline 22% to $37.1 million and adjusted EBITDA was $1.9 million The decline was driven by a decrease in both orders and average order size, which reinforces our belief that we need to pursue meaningful change. The type of change that we are committed to delivering. Fortunately, we are moving forward from a position of financial stability. We ended the first quarter with $13.7 million in cash, no debt and positive operating cash flow.

We also benefit from strong gross margins, a unique and highly differentiated product line, and a foundation of subscription based accounts. On our last call, I outlined 3 priorities needing attention. The brand, our consumer proposition, and operational excellence and productivity. Over the past 90 days, we have dug deeper and have concluded that we need a comprehensive strategy that reimagines our go-to-market approach our marketing engine, our competitive proposition, and our cost structure if we want to maximize our potential and be prepared to capture the opportunities that lie ahead. The goal is to transform LifeVantage into a brand driven, consumer focused company that leverages digital capabilities to create an expanding community of consumers, and brand advocates.

Our brand, lies at the heart of the transformation. Today, there are thousands of supplement companies essentially selling the same products with the same ingredients and the same benefits to the same consumers. Some offer different forms and features, but beyond their marketing campaigns, many are virtually indistinguishable. LifeVantage, on the other hand, can occupy a much more distinctive space. that is because LifeVantage is built around a fundamentally different proposition. Rather than simply giving the body more ingredients, more products, and more things to take, we develop products designed to work with the body's own biology and activate natural processes that are clinically proven to improve people's health. That distinction lies at the heart of what differentiates LifeVantage.

And it positions the company in a new growing, and ownable white space as the next generation of health and science. Of course, the challenge is to take our differentiated approach to health and science and turn it into a differentiated consumer proposition, and ultimately a differentiated brand. that is the starting point of our strategic roadmap which has 3 major components. The first strategic building block focuses on repositioning the company to change the way people think about LifeVantage and to give consumers a reason to care about the brand. That means repositioning LifeVantage as a next generation nutraceutical company. That positioning builds on our product's unique ability to activate the body's powerful biological systems to improve people's health.

To get started, we are launching a new campaign based on groundbreaking new research that shows how our lead product Protandim NRF2, activates the body's natural defense system to protect the body from environmental toxins like microplastics, pesticides, pollution, and more. For the first time, the new campaign uses before and after images that show the positive impact Protandim has on cells affected by specific environment toxins. it is an exciting new approach designed to create emotional connection with the brand We start with an important consumer outcome which, in this case, is to protect the body from environmental toxins, and we follow-up with simple to understand visuals that provide scientific proof.

Our second strategic building block focuses on reimagining the business proposition. To make it easier to discover, engage with, and share LifeVantage. Our approach is to modernize the business build new capabilities, and align with the way consumers shop and buy today. To be clear, we are focusing on rethinking the selling proposition to make it simpler, more digital, and more attractive while at the same time reimagining the consumer journey to strengthen acquisition, retention, referrals, and social engagement. In the second quarter of calendar year 27, we will launch our new website and a more modern digital platform in North America. Followed by a third quarter 2027 launch of a new consumer driven business suite for sellers.

Our goal is to combine the reach and convenience of an integrated digital ecosystem with the affinity that comes from a community capable of driving engagement around the brand. Our third strategic building block focuses on expanding beyond our current scale and scope to more aggressively penetrate key markets expand share in high potential categories, and identify new growth platforms. I am not going to discuss details here to preserve our strategic interests, However, the overriding principle is focus. We need to become more selective about where we compete and where we invest.

Now I want to be thoughtful about expectations. it is still early, but we realize we need to reset the economics of the business by creating a more focused, tighter organization with improved efficiency. That work is progressing, so I am not gonna get ahead of it, and we are not providing formal guidance today. But shareholders should understand that our transformation agenda addresses both sides of the value creation equation. Finally, before turning the call over to Carl to cover Q1 financials, I want to touch on an additional item that will help our ability to build momentum and strength as we execute our strategy. Starting January 1, 2027, our fiscal year will align with the calendar year.

That means we will have 1 calendar for strategy, planning, budgeting, incentives, innovation, commercial activation, and performance management. it is a relatively simple change with significant implications for how we run the company. And the timing is appropriate as January 1st marks the beginning of the next generation of the company that we are building. With that, I would like to turn the call over to Carl so he can walk you through our financial results in more detail. Carl?

We delivered net revenue of $37.1 million in the current quarter, which was down 22% compared to $47.6 million in the same period a year ago. The decrease was primarily driven by continued downward pressure in the number of orders from our active consumer base and lower average order size reflecting impacts from the broader macroeconomic environment as well as lower sales from our MindBody GLP-1 System.

These declines were partially offset by sales of the LoveBiome product line which we acquired in October 2025. Revenue in the Americas region decreased 22.2% to $29 million and revenue in the Asia Pacific and Europe region decreased 21.2% to $8.2 million including $400 thousand or 3.9% of the negative impact from foreign currency rate fluctuations. Subscription based revenue continues to provide a substantial portion of our revenue in the quarter. Representing more than 75% of total revenue.

We also recognize another quarter of improvement in our retention metrics for both consultants and customers in comparison to the prior year period. Our gross profit percentage for the quarter was 75.4%, compared to 79.5% in the prior year period, reflecting higher inventory obsolescence expenses along with higher shipping and warehouse expenses. Excluding the additional inventory allowance related to our MindBody product line, adjusted non GAAP gross profit percentage was 78.2%.

Commissions and incentive expense was 41.4% of revenue, compared to 43.5% a year ago primarily due to the timing and magnitude of promotional and incentive programs changes in revenue mix, and changes in the mix of customers and independent consultants. Selling, general, and administrative expenses were 34.3% of revenue, compared to 31.2% in the prior year period, reflecting the overall decrease in net revenue. As Terrence mentioned earlier, we understand the need to reset the economics of the business and are in the process of carefully reviewing all SG&A spend to become more focused and efficient. GAAP operating loss was $100 thousand compared to operating income of $2.3 million in the prior year period.

Adjusted non GAAP operating income was 900 thousand compared to $2.5 million a year ago. We also maintain access to a $5 million revolving line of credit with no balance outstanding as of the end of the quarter.

Capital expenditures were $1.2 million during the quarter, compared to $400 thousand in the prior year period, primarily reflecting our continued investment in technology infrastructure including investment in our new e commerce platform. We also recently announced a quarterly cash dividend of $05 per share of common stock that will be paid on December 15, 2026, to shareholders of record as of December 1, 2026. We remain committed to our balanced capital allocation strategy in order to maximize shareholder value.

From a reporting standpoint, as Terrence noted, we are changing our fiscal year to align with the calendar year. For the 6 month transition period ending 12/31/2026, in addition to reporting quarterly results, will also file a Form 10-KT including audited financial statements in the first quarter of calendar year 27. Our new 2027 fiscal year will begin on January 1, 2027. Given the recent transition in our chief executive officer role, and our change in fiscal year, we are not issuing formal guidance on today's call. And with that, let me turn the call back over to Terrence. Terrence?

#3061. What Tech Leaders Get Wrong About AI Restructuring And Morale

AI is pushing tech companies to rethink how they organize teams, assign work and plan for the future. However, while an AI-driven restructuring plan may promise greater productivity and a stronger competitive position, those benefits don’t necessarily make the changes easy for employees to navigate.

For leaders, the challenge isn’t just deciding what needs to change; it’s managing how those changes affect the people expected to carry them out. Below, members of Forbes Technology Council discuss leadership mistakes that can damage employee morale during AI-driven restructuring, even when the business rationale is sound.

One mistake is asking employees to embrace AI while making them audition for their own survival. If showing you how to automate their work puts their jobs at risk, you’ve made hiding knowledge a rational response. Be explicit about what is changing; “AI made us do it” is an abdication of command. You cannot demand adaptability from your people while outsourcing your own accountability. - Frederik Gregaard, Cardano Foundation

The mistake is leading with the math, not the mission. Announce that “this role gets automated,” and people check out, even when the logic is airtight. At Agiloft, we never mandated AI. Instead, we showed the work: weekly demos, real wins and leaders doing it alongside everyone else. People don’t resist AI; they resist being told to adopt it without seeing why it’s worth it. - Eric Laughlin, Agiloft

Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

The biggest mistake a leader can make is to not bring employees along on the AI journey. Leaders who intentionally bring their entire workforce on this journey can pilot new technologies more broadly, implement rules and processes faster, and foster an organizational culture of innovation. At MetLife, we deploy a federated, CEO-led AI strategy where the ability to adapt is centered on our employees’ appetite to learn, unlearn and relearn skills at scale. - Bill Pappas, MetLife

Make a clear distinction between what AI will be utilized for and where human intervention and decision making will still be paramount. Do not use a “replace the process using AI and increase efficiency” narrative across the board. It can create job insecurity and bring down morale. Instead, get the workforce trained on the safe use of AI, and help them think about where they can bring efficiency into their own roles. - Komal Goyal, 6e Technologies

Don’t perpetuate AI hype. Contrived fear-mongering is suffocating, and leaders who either knowingly or unwittingly succumb to it kill their credibility with their teams, their stakeholders and their customers. The hype- and fear-based mania takes various forms, including elimination of jobs, industries and companies. Leaders who cannot separate fact from hype are starting to stand out in most undesirable ways. - Ricardo Madan, TEKsystems Global Services

The biggest mistake is asking people to automate their work without clearly explaining what their roles will be in the future. It risks each “efficiency boost” via AI being seen by employees as a signal that they are needed less and less, which is naturally a big hit to morale. Leaders need to give their people a clear plan and opportunities to contribute to the decisions and changes being made. - Roman Eloshvili, XData Group

The critical mistake is treating employee hesitation as stubborn obstruction rather than recognizing the natural friction between established tradecraft and emergent tools. When leaders dismiss anxiety as mere drag, they alienate the domain experts whose judgment and institutional trust are essential to navigating the transition. - Sean Maday, Game Plan Tech

One mistake is restructuring work around AI without restructuring career paths. The routine tasks AI can automate are often the same tasks through which employees build experience and prepare for more complex roles. Remove that work without creating new ways to develop, and people may stop seeing a future for themselves in the organization. Leaders need to show not only how work will change but also how employees can continue to grow as it does. - Klaudia Zaika, Apriorit LLC

The biggest mistake is announcing the “what” without a plan for the “who.” When AI is framed only as cost cutting, people see it as an enemy. Leaders must share a different mindset: AI is an ally that helps us improve in our roles and deliver more—and better—work. Pair every change with reskilling, and help teams bring AI into their day-to-day work. People commit when they see themselves in the future. - Maritza Diaz, ITJ USA, Inc.

The mistake is letting actions contradict the message. If AI is about productivity and not headcount reduction, prove it: Invest in training, give people time to adapt, and redeploy talent into value-added work. When employees see leadership follow through on what they’ve promised, they lean in. When they don’t, trust breaks, and every AI initiative after that encounters resistance instead of adoption. - Samuel Martinez, SDG Group

The most damaging mistake is announcing the AI strategy without redesigning the work. Leaders explain why AI matters, then leave teams to figure out on their own which tasks change, who decides what and how performance will be measured. People rarely lose morale because of change. They lose it because of ambiguity. When the old process stays in place and AI is layered on top, employees end up doing both jobs, and the technology starts to feel like a threat instead of relief. - Alessio Alionco, Pipefy

One of the most serious mistakes tech leaders can make is rushing to implement AI tools without the necessary safeguards and governance measures in place. If employees see their leaders creating unnecessary vulnerabilities by introducing poorly managed AI solutions without a plan in place to secure them, it sends a damaging message that harms morale and erodes faith in leadership. If those vulnerabilities lead to negative outcomes, that faith can be hard to win back. - Peter Garraghan, Mindgard

Don’t project certainty you don’t have. Leaders often don’t yet know how every role will change, so they either go quiet or promise too much; both erode trust once reality diverges. Say plainly what has been decided, what hasn’t, and when people will hear more. Then involve teams in redesigning their own work; the people doing it often see first where AI truly helps. - Kuldeep Chowhan, Walmart

A huge mistake is positioning AI as a competitor to human roles. Most human roles will be redesigned because of AI, not completely replaced. The relationship between people and AI is that of a tango: It requires rhythm, balance and trust. Positioning AI as a collaborator and focusing on getting the human side ready to work with AI is the best recipe for getting people engaged with the initiative to make AI work, even when the business case is not clear. - John Kostoulas, Dayforce

One leadership mistake is treating AI restructuring as a business decision that only needs to be explained, rather than as a human transition that needs to be led. Employees can understand the need for change, but vague communication and prolonged uncertainty make people feel disposable. Clarity, transparency and empathy are critical to maintaining trust and morale. - Nandish Dave, BitGo Inc.

One mistake is cutting the entry-level rung because AI now handles junior work. Every senior engineer built judgment on that kind of work. Remove the rung, and mid-level staff see a ladder with nobody climbing behind them, while seniors wonder who will ever succeed them. Redesign junior roles around reviewing and correcting AI output, and count that review work toward promotion so that the pipeline keeps producing the experts who will someday check what the AI gets wrong. - Kuan Archer, Archer Innovative Solutions Group, LLC

It’s a mistake to believe that AI exists in a vacuum. In fact, the applications of AI with the best business outcomes are those that have been implemented under the strategic guidance and management of talented human beings. Morale is murdered if employees believe that they’re being undervalued and are expendable, when in fact the opposite is true. - Scott Burgess, Continu

One of the biggest leadership mistakes is treating AI transformation as a technology journey rather than as a people journey. No matter how compelling the business case may be, leaders must engage employees early, communicate openly and empower them to participate in the change. For example, when automating a function, leaders could have employees participate in the change process, identifying where AI can augment their capabilities so they are not casualties of it. - Babajide Ojuola, International Energy Services Limited

#3059. The midterm election could reshape the muni bond market. Here’s what investors need to know

The outcome of Tuesday's election is expected to have broad implications across the market, including municipal bonds.

The spotlight has been on the battle for congressional control and whether Democrats will wrest the House of Representatives, the Senate or both from Republicans. But for the muni market, what happens at the state level could have bigger repercussions — at least in the near term.

There is an array of initiatives on ballots around the nation that could change tax laws and add to bond supply. Taxes matter to muni investors since the income received is free of federal tax, as well as state tax if the holder lives in the state where the bond is issued.

Depending on the location, ballot measures are up for approval that would either provide tax breaks, or raise taxes on the wealthy.

"It's a complete bifurcation between red and blue states," said Dan Close, head of municipals at Nuveen. "Blue states are trying to put in place graduated income tax structures, trying to capture more revenue from high-income earners. Red states are promoting affordability by trying to cut property taxes."

Red states are those that predominantly vote Republican, while blue states swing toward Democrats.

For instance, California has a proposition known as the "billionaire tax," which would impose a one-time levy equal to 5% of the wealth of certain taxpayers with at least $1 billion in assets. The state also has a measure on the ballot that would make a temporary tax hike permanent on individuals earning over $371,000, adjusted annually for inflation. The tax is currently set to expire in 2031.

"The impact to the muni bond market will be to make the exemption more valuable," Close said of the possible passage of tax increases. Investors will likely seek shelter in the muni market, which would send bond prices higher, he noted.

It is a different story in Florida, where voters are set to decide whether to increase the Sunshine State's homestead exemption for non-school district property taxes. Qualified homeowners currently have a $25,000 property tax exemption, as well as another for $25,000 that doesn't apply to school property taxes. The new proposal raises the latter exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 by 2028. New residents have a five-year waiting period before receiving the benefit.

If passed, some local governments will have to find other revenue sources or increase the overall tax rate to replace what they've lost, said Tom Kozlik, head of public policy and municipal strategy at HilltopSecurities.

"It's not necessarily going to result in downgrades for sure, but there would have to be some balancing with regard to overall revenues," he said.

Not all municipalities will be hurt equally, which means credit research is important, said Close.

"Like everything in municipal finance, it is really on a case-by-case basis that you could have some credit deterioration from [a] rollback of property taxes," he said.

Other voters on Tuesday will be asked to approve more state or local government debt. That could weigh on a market that has already seen heightened supply.

Some $473.8 billion has already been issued year to date, through September, according to the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association. That's a 7.8% increase over the same period a year ago. In 2025, total muni issuance reached $587.3 billion, 14.3% higher than 2024, Sifma said.

Cooper Howard, director of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research, believes supply is the biggest issue coming out of the election.

"That amount of issuance has been one of the reasons why you have to see that strong amount of demand continue to keep pace with it for total returns to keep up," Howard said.

Fortunately, new supply doesn't necessarily come quickly into the market. "There's a window over a couple years that they can issue," he noted.

The ultimate makeup of the next Congress could also have consequences for muni investors as lawmakers sort out their priorities. Most notable is what lawmakers will do to tackle the country's affordability problem, Kozlik at Hilltop said.

"There could be some tax policy initiatives and even affordability-related initiatives that manifest themselves in the first quarter of next year," he said. "That could impact housing. It could impact higher education. It could impact public power financing."

Investors considering moves before the election may want to look at those states with tax increases on the ballot, said Close at Nuveen.

For instance, Nuveen recently began offering a separately managed account dedicated to Washington after getting an enormous number of inquiries from financial advisors. The state recently enacted a 9.9% tax on individuals with taxable annual income above $1 million, set to go into effect in 2028. But the issue is now being put to voters, who can decide whether to repeal the new law.

"At the margin, if you do think that some of these measures are going to pass, knowing that bonds usually move up with an increase in taxes, there might be some opportunities to buy ahead of the election for blue states," Close said.

Howard believes munis are attractive right now, particularly for those who are in a tax bracket of 24% or above. Fundamentals are good and the bonds largely have good credit quality, he said. "About 70% of the broad muni index is either triple-A or double-A rated."

Kozlik is also bullish, calling yields "really attractive." He suggests investors concentrate on AA-rated or higher bonds.

"The muni space is part of the portfolio that most investors want," he said. "It helps them sleep well at night."

#3056. SIGA (SIGA) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Zero debt and a new Canadian deal stand out, but U.S. contract timing remains unclear.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

SIGA Technologies, Inc. (SIGA +5.16%) reported financial results for the third quarter and nine months ended Sept. 30, 2026, marking the completion of its product delivery obligations under the BARDA 19C contract. Management reported that the company is currently focused on securing a new procurement contract with the U.S. government, though the timing of such an award remains uncertain. The company indicated an expansion of its international customer base through a new five-year agreement with the Canadian Department of National Defence and is in advanced negotiations with another international customer. Strategic updates included a timeline revision for the Post-Exposure Prophylaxis supplemental NDA and the upcoming completion of a Phase I pediatric study.

Operator: Welcome to the SIGA Business Update Call. Before we turn the call over to SIGA management, please note that any forward-looking statements made during this call are based on management's current expectations and observations, and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ from forward-looking statements. SIGA does not undertake any obligation to update publicly any forward-looking statement to reflect events or changed circumstances after this call.

For a discussion of factors that could cause results to differ, please see the company's filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including without limitation, the company's annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31st, 2025, and its subsequent reports on Form 10-Q and Form 8-K. With that, I will turn the call over to Diem Nguyen, Chief Executive Officer of SIGA. Diem?

Diem Nguyen: Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining today's call to review our business results. I am joined by Dan Luckshire, our Chief Financial Officer, and we appreciate this opportunity to provide an update on our company. After the update, we will take your questions. Throughout 2026, SIGA has continued to execute on its core mission of working alongside governments to build and sustain long-term preparedness against potential biological threats, namely smallpox. We remain committed to positioning our smallpox therapeutic, TPOXX, for rapid, large-scale deployment should an outbreak occur. As a reminder, in the second quarter, we completed our final product delivery under the BARDA 19C contract, fulfilling all our product obligations under that agreement.

We are proud of this partnership, proud of how we performed, and proud to have played an important role in strengthening the U.S. government's smallpox preparedness. We believe the case for preparedness against biological threats remains strong. Geopolitical tensions and advances in technology, including AI, are reshaping the threat landscape. Mitigating these risks requires proactive, sustained government investment in medical countermeasures stockpiles. In an emergency, ready access to medical countermeasures is essential to protect both civilians and war fighters. At the same time, a compelling case for preparedness does not always translate into predictable procurement.

As we discussed during our last call, the process to secure a new U.S. government contract has progressed more slowly than in the past, and the timing of an award remains uncertain. Even so, we remain confident that TPOXX has an important role in our nation's preparedness plans and that national security for medical countermeasures remain important to the U.S. government. Despite the lack of certainty as to timing and details, based on our discussions with key stakeholders, we continue to believe that a new procurement contract will be awarded. Turning to our international business, I would like to share news of recent contract that advances our efforts to maintain a diverse revenue stream and customer base.

Last month, we signed a contract to supply oral TPOXX to Canada's Department of National Defence, or CDND, over the next five years. This contract is valued up to approximately $15 million. It includes firm commitments about $9 million over the first three years, plus up to $6 million in options exercisable at CDND's discretion. This is CDND's second TPOXX contract. The first, awarded in April of 2020 for the purchase up to approximately $14 million of TPOXX, was completed in 2025. Canada continues to be one of the leaders in smallpox preparedness among our international customers, and we believe this award reflects that commitment. It also highlights another important point.

In a public health emergency, the men and women of the armed forces are often among the first called on to respond, so making sure they have access to smallpox antiviral is a key part of being prepared. Beyond this contract, we are continuing advanced discussions with other international customers, including one which we are in late-stage negotiations. We look forward to providing an update at the appropriate time. Moving to our development activities, I'd like to provide an update on our pediatric formulation and Post-Exposure Prophylaxis, or PEP, programs. We continue to expect results from phase I study of our pediatric formulation by year end, and those results will inform next steps.

If successful, this formulation, together with the oral and IV formulations, would extend TPOXX coverage across the full population, from infants to adults. Children are among the most vulnerable in an outbreak, and an improved pediatric formulation will give governments a more complete solution for their stockpiles. On the PEP program, we continue to work closely with our partners at the Department of War, FDA, and CDC, all of whom remain highly engaged with this program. We recently met with the FDA to review the program, including the immunogenicity sample analysis the CDC plans to conduct.

At that meeting, the FDA has asked us to perform additional validation and related laboratory work to help ensure the accuracy of results from the sample analysis. This work is important and requires time, and as a result, we now expect to file our supplemental NDA in 2028. While this delay is disappointing, it does not change our view on the relevance of this program. In an outbreak, the ability to use TPOXX as a PEP for our military, first responders, and others exposed to smallpox virus can help save lives.

Regarding our financial results, as I said in prior calls, our business is subject to inherent quarter-to-quarter variability, so our results are best viewed over a longer horizon than any single period. Over the first nine months of the year, product revenues totaled approximately $42 million, including sales to the U.S. government and customers in Asia-Pacific region and Europe. That breadth, together with the new CDND contract I talked about earlier, reflects the continued commitment of governments around the world to smallpox preparedness. Before I turn the call over to Dan, I want to recognize Dennis Hruby our Chief Scientific Officer, who is retiring today after three decades with SIGA.

When Dennis joined us in 1996, there was no approved treatment for smallpox. Today, TPOXX is approved in the U.S., Canada, the European Union, the U.K., and Japan. It has been sold to more than 30 countries and is maintained in stockpiles around the world. Dennis's scientific leadership shaped the achievement at every step, from early-stage research through approval. On behalf of everyone at SIGA, I want to thank Dennis for his contributions to our company and to global health security. We're very pleased that he will continue to support us in an advisory role.

In closing, SIGA has always been guided by its mission to ensure governments are prepared to protect their citizens from smallpox, and that mission is unchanged. While procurement processes are not predictable, we stand ready to work with our governments around the world, and we do so with a strong balance sheet, including $116 million in cash and no debt at the end of the quarter. As I said at the start of the call, we believe the case for preparedness remains strong. Smallpox and other high-consequence threats are serious, and emerging technologies have the potential to lower barriers to creating or misusing biologic agents.

With preparation, these threats can be mitigated, and TPOXX has a long history of helping governments meet smallpox threats. With that, I'll turn over to Dan to review our financial results in more detail. Dan?

Dan Luckshire: Thanks, Diem. As noted earlier in the call, the company's product-related revenues are $42 million for the nine months ended September 30th, 2026, with most of the revenues being recorded in the second quarter, reflecting the variable rhythm of SIGA's business model. Year-to-date product revenues include approximately $26 million of IV TPOXX deliveries to the U.S. Strategic National Stockpile and approximately $13 million of international sales to two international customers. For the third quarter, there are no product sales to customers. In addition to product-related revenues for the nine months ended September 30th, 2026, the company also has research and development revenues of approximately $7 million.

Of this total, approximately $1 million of the research and development revenues were earned in the third quarter. Pre-tax operating income for the nine months ended September 30th, 2026, which excludes interest income and taxes, is approximately $2 million. For the quarter, pre-tax operating loss is approximately $7 million. Net income for the nine months ended September 30th, 2026, is approximately $6 million. For the quarter, net loss is approximately $3 million. In turn, fully diluted income per share for the nine months ended September 30th, 2026, is $0.09 per share, while fully diluted loss per share for the quarter is $0.04 per share. The company continues to maintain a strong balance sheet.

At September 30th, 2026, the company had a cash balance of approximately $116 million and no debt. This concludes the financial update. At this point, I will turn the call back to Diem.

Diem Nguyen: Thank you, Dan. With that, we'd like to open the call for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin the question-and-answer session. Should you have a question, please press the star key followed by the number one on your touchtone phone. You will hear a prompt that your hand has been raised. Should you wish to decline from the polling process, please press the star key followed by the number two. One moment, please, while we assemble the queue. Your first question comes from Jyoti Prakash of Edison Group. Please go ahead.

Jyoti Prakash: Hi, good evening. Thank you for taking my questions. First of all, congratulations on the recent contract from the CDND. Just want to understand if this is the international opportunity which was highlighted during the Q2 call, and if there's another order still under discussion, because you did mention that you're in conversations. If there is an order under discussion, can we hear about it during the remainder of the year? Going back to the CDND order, can you provide some color on the delivery schedule, particularly if we can expect anything to be delivered within 2027?

In your question, you asked about, well, is there another order? As noted in our prepared remarks, there is another order. I wanted to also highlight that deliveries are expected to start in 2027. The contract has the firm orders I just talked about and also has options.

Jyoti Prakash: Thank you, Dan. That was very useful. My second question relates to recent developments and something which has been on people's minds is the results of the U.S. midterm elections. Do you foresee any implications of the results on biodefense funding priorities and possibly the timing of the U.S. RFP?

Diem Nguyen: Hi, Jyoti. This is Diem. Nice to hear your voice, and thanks for joining the call and this question. As it relates to the new contract process, we currently do not believe that midterm results will have any material impact on the nature or trajectory of this process beyond the typical transition period that follows any election.

Jyoti Prakash: Great. Thank you, Diem. Just going back to international growth, we noted that Bavarian Nordic recently secured a four-year smallpox vaccine contract with the U.K. government. Do you see any sort of implications of this on your recent discussions with the European authorities?

Diem Nguyen: Thanks, Jyoti. So Europe, like many countries and continents, go through multi-year transformational in terms of national security priorities and spending. In this particular environment, each country has its own dynamics and priorities and is moving at its own pace. Overall, yes, we do believe that there's increased focus on biodefense and smallpox preparedness. This has resulted in the spending like the U.K. contract you just mentioned. I would say historically, though, smallpox preparedness across Europe has largely been vaccine-centric. Part of our work supporting a shift towards a more comprehensive approach that pairs vaccines with antivirals, very much similar to the U.S. model, but we do recognize that changing this paradigm takes time.

Specifically for TPOXX, we are part of evolving conversations on stockpiling, both at the country and regional level. Now, Jyoti, for your second question on our European label, in certain cases, the change does require some additional discussion. While this can affect timing, we do not believe it changes the long-term opportunity in Europe for smallpox stockpiling. Notably, just as a gentle reminder, we recently renewed our TPOXX filings both in Europe as well as in U.K. for the treatment of smallpox, and we really look forward to working with our European counterparts in our preparedness efforts.

Jyoti Prakash: That's very helpful. Thanks, Diem. No further questions from my side.

Diem Nguyen: Thank you. Today, I'd like to thank everybody for making time to join us on today's call and for your ongoing interest in SIGA. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter. Have a good evening.
