#3054. Prediction Markets Are Arriving in Your Investing App, and That Makes Us Nervous

NerdWallet, Inc. is an independent publisher and comparison service, not an investment advisor. Its articles, interactive tools and other content are provided to you for free, as self-help tools and for informational purposes only. They are not intended to provide investment advice. NerdWallet does not and cannot guarantee the accuracy or applicability of any information in regard to your individual circumstances. Examples are hypothetical, and we encourage you to seek personalized advice from qualified professionals regarding specific investment issues. Our estimates are based on past market performance, and past performance is not a guarantee of future performance.

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. And while our site doesn’t feature every company or financial product available on the market, we’re proud that the guidance we offer, the information we provide and the tools we create are objective, independent, straightforward — and free.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us. This may influence which products we review and write about (and where those products appear on the site), but it in no way affects our recommendations or advice, which are grounded in thousands of hours of research. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews of their products or services. Here is a list of our partners.

Prediction markets are booming, but that doesn’t make them a sound investment strategy.

The investing information provided on this page is for educational purposes only. NerdWallet, Inc. does not offer advisory or brokerage services, nor does it recommend or advise investors to buy or sell particular stocks, securities or other investments.

Around this time every year, we conduct NerdWallet’s annual broker review process. We assess what’s changed in the industry, discuss which brokerage features matter most (and which ones now matter less), and finally, we do the work by opening accounts to test them.

Prediction markets, which have made their way into some of the most popular investing apps, came up more than we expected in testing this year.

At first, we decided to simply collect information on who does and doesn’t offer access to them, without intending to reward or penalize a broker either way. It would be a neutral presentation of facts, not something that would factor into how we scored a broker.

But one afternoon, all together in the office, we confronted an uncomfortable question: “Do prediction markets, and such easy access to them within an investment app, go against NerdWallet’s editorial house views?”

After careful consideration, we all agreed: they do.

So we started to configure our 2027 rubric with a firmer stance against this trendy feature, penalizing brokers that actively market sports and entertainment event contracts, and whose prediction markets come with few, if any, guardrails.

We’ve distilled our discussion down to three main points:

These products are being marketed alongside investments.

We fear they could be discouraging long-term investing.

Let’s start here: Many aspects of trading could be seen as gambling-adjacent. Options, futures, highly leveraged single-day equity bets and even crypto can all easily fall into the “highly speculative” category. So why are we picking on prediction markets in particular?

In our view, a key differentiator is a much lower barrier to entry with few in-app guardrails in place.

Most of the products we mentioned above require some level of fluency — and at times even permission from the broker — to dabble in. To trade options, for example, you need to answer questions about your investing proficiency, your finances and more. And even after approval, the terminology required to trade can be so intimidating that the language itself can become an indirect deterrent.

Event contracts, which form the backbone of prediction markets, are largely presented in the vernacular, and our testing showed approval to trade them is completed with a few taps from the home screen. Moreover, their content is often unrelated to finance — according to a May 2026 report by the Pew Research Center, around 80% of volume on the prediction market platform Kalshi was for sports events[1]Pew Research Center. Trading Volume on Prediction Markets Has Soared in Recent Months. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

Answering a binary question (yes/no; this/that), posed in everyday language about a familiar topic — something like, “Will the Knicks beat the Spurs on Sunday?” — can be far less daunting than figuring out what an options chain is or understanding forex pairs.

In other words, what makes prediction markets accessible to a wider audience is also what makes them problematic, especially when housed within an investing account. Which brings us to our next point.

On the platforms that feature them, we found that prediction markets almost always appear alongside stock and ETF trading. We think this is a mistake. What has made these mobile-first investing apps so good for so long (making it easy to move, manage and invest money through a beautiful interface) is what’s now making us nervous.

For example, most investing platforms let users do any number of smart things with idle cash. They could open an Individual Retirement Account (IRA), a custodial account or a robo-managed portfolio all through a single app. But now, they can dip into that same pot of money to bet on whether Beyoncé or Alicia Keys will play the Super Bowl halftime show.

But is anyone actually trading these event contracts? Let’s use data from publicly traded brokers that offer prediction markets to explore this.

In Q3 2026, Robinhood’s revenue from event contracts rose more than 600% year over year to $173 million, while the number of event contracts traded grew more than sevenfold to 16.4 billion[2]Robinhood. Robinhood Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources . This was the second-highest source of transaction revenue behind options trading. In a forecast reported on by Cointelegraph, Bernstein analysts projected Robinhood’s prediction markets could drive $1.7 billion in annual revenue by 2028[3]Yahoo Finance. Bernstein Sees Robinhood Prediction Markets Reaching $1.7 Billion in Revenue by 2028, Topping Crypto. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

Coinbase's Q1 2026 quarterly report called prediction markets “one of its fastest-scaling products ever, driven by strong retail interest[4]Coinbase. Coinbase Q1 Financial Results Show Resilient Financial Performance Driven by New All-Time High Crypto Trading Volume Market Share. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources ."

In a call discussing Webull’s Q2 results, U.S. CEO Anthony Denier noted trading volume in Webull’s nascent prediction market product grew about 70% quarter over quarter[5]Gloom. Webull (BULL) Q2 2026 earnings call transcript. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources .

Gemini’s Q2 report shows prediction market volume rose 93% quarter over quarter[6]Gemini. Shareholder Update Q2 2026. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

So, now that we’ve established that these markets are growing in popularity — and investing platforms appear to have a large incentive to lean into them — how are all those event contract traders faring? That brings us to our final point.

Is all this even worth it? Several studies show how hard it is to actually turn a profit in prediction markets. Here are a few:

One study, conducted by researchers at ESSEC Business School, HEC Montréal and the University of Toronto's Rotman School of Management, covered 2.4 million Polymarket accounts across $67 billion in trading volume between November 2022 and March 2026, and found that 69% of users lost money[7]SSRN. Who Wins and Who Loses In Prediction Markets? Evidence from Polymarket. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources . Moreover, the top 1% of users who made a profit accounted for about 76% of all gains. Translation: Even if you did turn a profit, there’s a good chance you didn’t make much.

A Bloomberg analysis supports this: From January 2025 to April 2026, more than 100,000 Polymarket accounts lost at least $1,000[8]Bloomberg. Most Prediction Market Traders Are Losing Money While Bots Rack Up Gains. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources . Of the 2 million active wallets studied, almost half made or lost less than $10 during the period, while far fewer accounts collected larger profits.

A separate Wall Street Journal analysis echoed the same trend: 67% of Polymarket profits go to 0.1% of accounts, and more than 70% of Polymarket users lost money[9]The Wall Street Journal. Why Almost Everyone Loses—Except a Few Sharks—on Prediction Markets. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources .

While there is far less data available on Kalshi trades (Polymarket runs on a public blockchain, making it easy to extract and analyze data), a Kalshi spokesperson confirmed in the Wall Street Journal analysis above that one month of data in 2026 showed there were 2.9 unprofitable users to each profitable user[10]Wall Street Journal. Why Almost Everyone Loses—Except a Few Sharks—on Prediction Markets. Accessed Nov 10, 2026. View all sources .

The first study above discusses how event contract trading is binary and zero-sum: If one trader wins, another loses. This means traders allocating money to these instruments could be missing out on aspects of equity markets that have helped create long-term wealth for previous generations.

“Unlike equity markets, there is no equity premium, no dividends, and no passive investment options. Their short maturities naturally encourage short-horizon trading, which is precisely what the behavioral finance literature has suggested is most destructive to wealth accumulation. Given the rapid growth of these platforms and their role as a potential entry point for young investors, understanding who bears the losses has direct implications for investor welfare and market regulation.”

As a reminder, the vast majority of Polymarket users bore the losses.

At NerdWallet, our mission has always been to help people make smarter financial decisions, so we’re sticking by that. Starting with our 2027 ratings, brokers that offer easy access to sports and entertainment event contracts will lose points in our scoring system because we believe this new product has the potential to harm long-term wealth building and doesn’t belong in investing platforms.

So, what’s a better way forward? Bring back the friction and make prediction markets a separate app. Financial institutions, businesses and individuals can still explore legitimate use cases for prediction markets, such as forecasting and hedging. And we’re not here to stop anyone from trading event contracts for entertainment with extra money. We just don’t want these markets so easily conflated with the legitimate investing vehicles these apps already offer. And our reviews will reflect that.

#3043. Lincoln Educational (LINC) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Student starts jumped as management raised its full-year revenue outlook.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Lincoln Educational Services Corporation (LINC +24.57%) reported results for the third quarter of 2026, including double-digit growth in revenue and student starts. Management stated that performance was driven by improved lead conversion rates and the expansion of campus facilities. The company revised its full-year revenue guidance upward while narrowing its student start growth targets. Strategic initiatives centered on new campus developments in New York, Maryland, and Arizona, alongside a focus on high-demand skilled trades and healthcare programs. Management also emphasized capital allocation through share repurchases and the acquisition of the Melrose Park campus facility.

Operator: Thank you for standing by and welcome to the Lincoln Educational Services Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in listen-only mode. After the speaker's presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during this session, you will need to press star one on your telephone. If your question has been answered and you would like to remove yourself from the queue, simply press star one again. As a reminder, today's program is being recorded. Now I would like to introduce your host for today's program, Doug Sherk of the EVC Group. Please go ahead, sir.

Before the market opened today, Lincoln Educational Services issued a news release reporting financial results for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, ending September 30th, 2026, as well as recent corporate developments. The release is available on the investor relations portion of the company's corporate website at www.lincolntech.edu. Joining us today on the call are Scott Shaw, President Chief Executive Officer, and Brian Meyers, Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer, and Treasurer. Today's call is being recorded and is being broadcast live on the company's website. A replay of the call will be archived on the company's website.

Statements made by Lincoln's management on today's call regarding the company's business that are not historical facts may be forward-looking statements as the term is identified in federal securities laws. All forward-looking statements are qualified in their entirety by this cautionary statement, and Lincoln undertakes no obligation to publicly revise or update any forward-looking statement, whether as a result of new information, future events, or otherwise, after the date thereof. One other housekeeping matter.

During the Q&A portion of the call today, we would ask questioners to limit themselves to two questions and then requeue to ask any additional questions. In advance, we thank you for your cooperation. Now I would like to turn the call over to Scott Shaw, President Chief Executive Officer of Lincoln Educational Services.

Scott Shaw: Thank you, Doug, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today as we review our strong third quarter financial and operating performance and provide an update on recent business developments that position us to continue our growth for the remainder of the year and into the future. Before I begin my comments about our quarter, I would like to wish everyone a happy Veterans Day, which is this Wednesday, November 11th. Lincoln was founded to help World War II veterans returning home transition into civilian careers. Today, we'd like to commemorate our legacy by thanking our past and current military members and their families for their service and sacrifice and wishing them all a happy Veterans Day.

Last month, we celebrated Lincoln's 80th anniversary of providing superior education and training services for safe, in-demand, rewarding careers. As we did back in 1946, Lincoln continues to lead the way in an evolving skilled trades marketplace. Today, we are benefiting from the expanding interest across America as the demand for skilled workers exceeds supply. To meet the demand, we are expanding our programs at existing campuses and developing new campuses. We have focused our strategies on simplifying operations to maximize graduate opportunities in the electrical, HVAC, automotive, welding, and healthcare fields. These careers are in high demand and are expected to remain in high demand for many years despite the effects of artificial intelligence deployment throughout American enterprises.

Our third quarter performance illustrates the success of our established model. We regained our student start growth momentum by generating a 14.2% increase over the prior year period. This growth resulted from our team successfully responding to a rapidly evolving marketing environment, increasing our conversion of leads to starts, examining new channels, benefiting from investments in our high school channel, and consistently exploring ways to increase large language model inclusion of our differentiation and superior outcomes for skilled trades and in-demand career training and education.

Demand for our high return on investment training and education programs remains strong as corporations and organizations throughout America continue to search for ways to close their seemingly chronic employee skills gap, which is inhibiting their growth. We believe the demand for our programs is also benefiting from Americans increasingly turning to the skilled trades to provide stable, rewarding long-term careers. Our strong student starts, as well as the increase in our average student population, led to solid double-digit revenue growth for the quarter.

By continuing to realize operating efficiencies from our Lincoln 10.0 hybrid teaching platform and other initiatives, we generated a substantial increase in cash generated from operating activities, a 22.5% increase in operating income, and more than 30% growth in adjusted EBITDA. And we returned capital to our shareholders through the purchase of approximately 870,000 shares of our common stock during the third quarter. Our decision to repurchase shares and our board's recent decision to increase the authorization to a total of $70 million reflects our confidence in Lincoln Tech's long-term growth prospects and our belief that our stock represents an attractive investment opportunity.

The increased authorization combined with our strong liquidity position and expected cash flow generation provides us with the ability to continue investing in our growth initiatives while also returning capital to shareholders. Brian will provide more detail on the repurchases and our capital allocation strategy in his remarks. The Lincoln 10.0 hybrid teaching platform continues to provide flexibility to students needing to balance work and life while earning their certificate or degree. We have achieved this flexibility by combining hands-on learning at campus facilities with a component of classroom work delivered through online instruction, which reduces the time needed to complete many of our curriculums and accelerates our graduates to their highly rewarding careers.

While our Lincoln 10.0 hybrid teaching platform is realizing instructional efficiencies for the company, our instructors, and our students, we are also continuing to invest some of the gains from these efficiencies in programs and processes to continuously drive improved student outcomes, which we believe is positively impacting our student retention rate at our programs open for more than a year. Our strong cash generation and enhanced liquidity through an expanded credit facility provides ample resources to fund these initiatives, as well as new campus development and program expansions. During the third quarter, we completed the development of our new Hicksville, New York campus, which will start its first class this month.

The 65,000 sq ft state-of-the-art campus in the heart of Long Island is offering specialized career training in automotive, welding, HVAC, and electrical and electronics, and is the second Lincoln campus in New York, as well as the 11th in the greater New York, Connecticut, and New Jersey tri-state area. During the quarter, we also continued the development of our Rowlett, Texas campus and initiated the development of our first Arizona campus in Tempe. We also initiated the development of our first focus program campus in the metropolitan Washington, D.C. area.

Located in Suitland, Maryland, the 36,000 sq ft facility will initially offer electrical and electrical systems technology and HVAC programs to address the high demand for employees trained in these fields from data center and other employers in the region. The focus program concept is enabling Lincoln to develop the Suitland campus for an estimated $10 million investment compared to the $25 million investment we need to make when creating a traditional build-out. The campus is expected to serve approximately 500 students and generate some $15 million in annual revenues and $5 million in EBITDA when fully ramped up. We have also recently completed expansion of two other highly successful campuses.

At our East Point, Georgia campus, we added 15,000 sq ft to serve an additional 300 students, bringing the total facility capacity to approximately 70,000 sq ft. The East Point campus continues to excel in all aspects of its operations, and together with our Marietta campus, illustrates the marketing leverage and efficiencies we can achieve in markets with more than one location. Our other expansion took place at the Melrose Park, Illinois campus, where we ended our auto collision program, introduced our HVAC program, created our third Tesla training center, expanded our welding program, and bought the facility.

The successful transition means our average student population at Melrose Park has grown to the point where the campus is now the second largest in the Lincoln system, and we have achieved this growth while reducing our facility cost. Some of our recent operating highlights at existing campuses include the teaching out of the collision program at our Grand Prairie campus, where we expect to expand other programs as we've done in Melrose Park, continued strong growth in high school starts throughout our system, consistent graduation and job placement rates, and positive reaccreditation visits at a number of our campuses.

Our efforts to revitalize our healthcare programs continue to generate results as student starts and graduation rates are realizing positive trends. We also made further progress in reducing our bad debt as a percentage of revenues, as well as improving our financial aid processing, which has played a key role in resuming double-digit start growth. As I mentioned at the beginning of my comments, we also improved our lead conversion rate as compared to historical levels, and despite higher lead generation costs, maintained a relatively flat overall student acquisition cost during the third quarter. Our business development team continues to examine underserved markets across the U.S. that would benefit from Lincoln's proven career development programs.

We also continue to explore partnerships with organizations to bring high value-added career training that plays a critical role in reducing the skills gap. During the quarter, we celebrated the 500th graduate of our Johnson Controls Academy and expanded our WorkforceLinc division's collaboration with CMC Corporation. In addition, WorkforceLinc formed a new partnership with the engineering firm ABB, a global leader in electrification and automation, which will support ABB in building a nationwide recurring source of electrical and electronic technician candidates. A major focus of the effort is to develop skilled employees to serve the maintenance needs of the nation's growing number of data centers.

Overall, it's been a very productive quarter for Lincoln Tech, which is reflected in the company's financial performance momentum. As we look ahead to the remainder of the year, we're encouraged by our start to the fourth quarter. The need for employees trained in the skilled trades, automotive, and healthcare fields continue to expand at robust rates, and Lincoln Tech is providing a unique, proven education and training model to meet the demand for our talented men and women to enter stable, rewarding careers that can last a lifetime.

We are continuously working to increase the visibility of our outcomes and differentiation from other less successful training models, and our third quarter performance and outlook for the full year increases our confidence in achieving our 2030 financial objectives of approximately $850 million in revenue and $150 million in EBITDA. Before I turn the call over to Brian, I'd like to note that we will be continuing our investor outreach efforts over the next few months. We have an exciting story to share as demand remains strong, so we plan to attend conferences, conduct non-deal roadshows with our covering analysts, along with other events such as campus tours.

We will be in Dallas attending the Southwest IDEAS Conference on November 18th, in Minneapolis and Chicago on November 23rd and 24th, respectively, with Lake Street, and in New York City with Barrington in early December. Additionally, we will be attending the Northland Virtual Conference on December 16th and the Needham Annual Growth Conference in New York City on January 12th and 13th. Now I'll turn the call over to Brian Meyers so he can review the financial highlights for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 and review our guidance. Brian?

Brian Meyers: Thank you, Scott, and good morning, everyone. I'll begin with a few recent developments, including our capital allocation priorities and recent share repurchase activity before reviewing our third quarter 2026 financial results and provide an update on our outlook for the remainder of the year. In 2022, our board established a share repurchase program as a way to return capital to shareholders when we believe repurchases are an attractive use of capital, consistent with our overall capital allocation priorities. First and foremost, we invest in the business, which we continue to do, and I'll cover in more details when I review our expansion activities and capital investments. Second, we maintain a strong balance sheet.

At the end of the quarter, we had more than $135 million of liquidity. Third, we seek to return excess capital to shareholders over time. As Scott mentioned, during the quarter, we repurchased approximately 871,000 shares of common stock for a total cost of approximately $21 million. Given our strong liquidity, cash flow generation, the board has extended the share repurchase program through May 2028 and increased the authorization by $30 million, bringing the remaining capacity to over $37 million. The timing and amounts of any future repurchase will depend on market conditions, share price, our capital needs, and other factors.

The program does not obligate us to acquire any particular number of shares and may be modified, suspended, or discontinued at any time. In November, we also amended our revolving credit facility to provide greater flexibility, including supporting future share repurchases, which I'll discuss in more detail later in my remarks. Now let's turn to the third quarter financial results. As a reminder, as we have noted in prior earnings calls, there was a shift in our academic calendar last year that resulted in the start class that typically occurs in late June moving to July 1st, 2025.

To provide a meaningful comparison, as in prior quarters, we have adjusted the third quarter 2025 student starts to exclude those July 1st starts and treat them as if they occurred in last year's second quarter. Our discussions today will compare third quarter 2026 starts with those adjusted numbers. We delivered strong financial and operating results in the third quarter, highlighted by solid growth in student starts, revenue, adjusted EBITDA, net income, and continued adjusted EBITDA margin expansion. Demand for our programs remains strong as reflected in our student start growth of 14.2%. Our ending student population grew by approximately 2,100 students, or 11% year-over-year, providing a solid foundation for continued revenue growth.

Organic student starts increased by nearly 5%, reflecting continued demand for our programs. Our measurement of organic growth includes new campuses and programs that were in place for more than one year. The additional start growth over prior year came from our program expansions and our new Houston campus, which continues to grow its student population. As Scott discussed, actions we implemented to improve conversion from leads to enrollment to start gain traction during the third quarter, contributing to student start growth and also benefiting our student acquisition cost. Cost per start for the quarter remained relatively flat despite elevated lead costs, reflecting the benefits of improved lead conversion. This performance exceeded our expectations.

Our strong student start volume and our efforts to improve enrollment conversions offset the higher spend in the quarter, and we are encouraged by this progress. However, we do expect that cost per start will be elevated above prior year levels in the near term as these initiatives continue. Year-to-date, student starts had increased 1,864 or 11%. Based on current enrollment trends, we expect this performance to continue, which supports our outlook for the full year student start growth of 10%-12%. Third quarter revenue increased 12.6% to $159.2 million, driven primarily by a 10.9% increase in our average student population. This marks our 14th consecutive quarter of double-digit year-over-year revenue growth. Turning to profitability.

Operating expenses for the quarter were consistent with our expectations. Corporate expenses were relatively flat, while campus-level expenses increased in line with our revenue growth, supporting our larger student population and continued growth initiatives. This expense growth was primarily offset by favorable bad debt expense, which continues as a percentage of revenue below prior year levels, reflecting our continued focus on collections and managing credit losses. Adjusted EBITDA increased 30.8% to $17.4 million, with our adjusted EBITDA margin expanding by 150 basis points to approximately 11%. This improvement reflects operating leverage from our larger student population. As a reminder, beginning in 2026, our calculation of adjusted EBITDA no longer adds back pre-opening and first-year operating losses from new campuses.

During the quarter, we incurred $2 million in new campus losses compared to $2.7 million the prior year quarter. These costs are fully reflected in our reported adjusted EBITDA, highlighting our ability to deliver strong earnings growth while continuing to invest in our campus expansion strategies. Net income increased 24% to $4.7 million compared to $3.8 million the prior year quarter. Diluted earnings per share were $0.15 based on approximately 31.4 million weighted average diluted shares outstanding. Turning to capital expenditures. We continue to invest in future business opportunities. Year-to-date spending totaled approximately $69.6 million, of which $67.4 million is reflected in our statement of cash flows, with the remainder accrued but not yet paid.

Third quarter capital expenditures of approximately $36.4 million were in line with our expectations, including $17.4 million related to the purchase of our previously leased Melrose Park campus. We continue to expect full-year capital expenditures of $95 million-$100 million, consistent with our previously communicated outlook. Turning now to our balance sheet and financing activities. We continue to generate strong operating cash flow during the quarter, supported by our growing student population, improved operating performance, and effective management of cash collections. Cash flow from operations totaled $34.9 million in the third quarter, an increase of $11 million compared to the prior year quarter.

Year-to-date operating cash flow reached $61.5 million compared to $15.8 million in the prior year, representing an improvement of nearly $46 million. This increase reflects our improved operating performance, continued focus on working capital management. We ended the third quarter with $20.6 million in cash and $115 million available in our revolving credit facility, providing total liquidity of $135.6 million. At quarter end, we had $10 million outstanding under the credit facility. During the quarter, we also completed the purchase of our previously leased Melrose Park campus, financed primarily with a $15 million mortgage loan. This transaction reduced our ongoing facility costs while providing us with a long-term control of the property.

In November, we amended our $125 million revolving credit facility. The amendment expands our flexibility for future share repurchases, provided that we maintain total liquidity of more than $25 million following any repurchase. The amendment also adds a daily borrowing option that can be repaid at any time without penalty. In addition to our existing borrowing options, this lets us manage cash balances and borrowing costs more effectively. Together, these changes enhance our ability to employ capital, supporting our campus expansion initiatives while maintaining the flexibility to return capital to shareholders through our share repurchase program. Turning to our full-year outlook.

Based on our year-to-date results, current trends, we are raising our revenue guidance, narrowing our student start growth range, and reiterating our guidance for adjusted EBITDA, net income, diluted EPS, and capital expenditures. We now expect revenue of $600 million-$605 million, up from $590 million-$600 million, adjusted EBITDA of $76 million-$80 million, net income of $23 million-$26 million, diluted EPS of $0.74-$0.83, capital expenditures of $95 million-$100 million, and student start growth of 10%-12%, narrowed from 10%-14%. As I mentioned earlier, beginning in 2026, our calculation of adjusted EBITDA no longer excludes pre-opening and first-year operating losses from new campuses.

Accordingly, our guidance continues to include approximately $10 million in losses at our new campuses, which remain in line with our expectations. Non-cash stock-based compensation continues to be our only expense add-back to the calculation this year. Growth initiatives represent approximately 75% of our planned capital expenditures, underscoring our continued focus on expanding capacity and supporting future enrollment growth. We'll continue to update our capital expenditure outlook as we announce additional campus locations. In closing, our strong year-to-date performance reinforces our confidence in achieving our long-term financial objectives. Before we open the call for questions, I'd like to echo Scott's appreciation for the veterans throughout the Lincoln community and thank them for their services.

I also want to recognize our entire team for their continued dedication to providing a high-quality education and strong outcome to our students. With that, I'll turn the call over to the operator for questions. Operator?

Operator: Certainly. Ladies and gentlemen, we would like to ask you to please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. You may get back in the queue as time allows. Our first question comes on the line of Alex Paris from Barrington Research. Your question, please.

Alex Paris: Hi, guys. Thanks for taking my question, and thanks for the beat and limited raise. It is quite a change from some of the other education reports we had seen earlier last week and the week before, which has kind of driven down stock prices. I wanted to dig into starts guidance a little bit, just starts in general as well as starts guidance. You narrowed the guidance from 10%-14% growth for the full year to 10%-12%. I think most of the analysts that publish starts numbers were at the low end, including me anyway. The question is, what is going on with starts?

Then within starts, let us talk about high school, because we had pretty big expectations for high school this time around.

Scott Shaw: Sure, Alex, and thanks for the question. I mean, we are in many regards no different than others in that certainly the marketplace has changed with the searches taking place and maybe Google not being as effective. But we have a number of channels that we are deploying or utilizing or tapping into, which obviously turned into a really strong performance in the third quarter. As we also mentioned, we are getting better with our conversions, we are getting better with our financial aid process, we are getting better in connecting with the enrollments that we have.

I will just say this, compared to the second quarter, we have overcome those challenges, and that is what has helped lead us into a strong third quarter. We will continue down this path of finding improvements, trying to find new channels of opportunity, expanding our social media presence, while continuing to invest and make changes so that these large language models just do not focus solely on cost, but also will highlight what we know are those strong benefits of a Lincoln Tech education, such as better graduation rates, good return on investment, and the like. As you mentioned, we have made investments in our high school sales team, and they performed well for us.

They were at double digits growth, which is what we wanted, and we anticipate, frankly, next year to be more robust than this year, because as you also probably know, investing in high school takes time. But we have a really well-trained group of individuals that are committed to helping students. They're out there as we speak, going to those high schools, introducing the skilled trades. To the high school channel, we don't get any of the distractions that, I guess, exist out there with these large language models, because we can clearly demonstrate where the value is by coming to Lincoln Tech, and both the high school students and their parents can resonate very strongly with that message.

The landscape is constantly changing. We're constantly adapting to that landscape, and I'm just really pleased by the performance that our team is achieving.

Alex Paris: I guess that my follow-up would be, since you referred to it, you have a number of channels that you're tapping. So, high school is part of that, military is part of that, corporate alliances are part of that. Could you break down either total revenue or starts by those various channels, just ballpark at least?

Scott Shaw: Yeah. So, I mean, in aggregate, high school is about 20% of our starts, a little bit higher than that. Obviously, in the third quarters, that's where the bulk of the high school students come in. Military is still small for us. While we reference the fact that we started as 100% military back in 1946, we're only about 6% right now. But we've made investments also in our military channel that we anticipate seeing some benefits from, frankly, in 2027. So, it would be nice to bring that back up to hopefully double digits in the next 24 months.

Then from a corporate standpoint, I still believe that's a huge, really untapped opportunity for us and an area that we are going to put more resources behind. I think that once we tap into that fully, that will really help support our growth beyond just reaching the adults that we do through our existing marketing channels. So, we're just going to continue to find the people where they are, because we know from talking to employers that they have not let up on the need for what we're doing. So, it's really just trying to get our message out there to as many people as possible.

Alex Paris: Great. Thanks for the additional color, guys. I'll get back in the queue.

Operator: Thank you. Our next question comes from the line of Eric Wold from Texas Capital Securities. Your question, please.

Eric Wold: Two quick questions, I guess. First off, what are you seeing in terms of the cost per lead increase compared to last year? How is that running? Is it still up 20-ish percent? Then what are you finding is the best way to kind of navigate around that in terms of which channels, like social media, are kind of proving the most effective around that?

Scott Shaw: Sure. Yeah, we're still seeing cost per lead up at that level, Eric, around the 20% level, and that's what we're going to be forecasting going forward. We're hoping that will lessen in time, but as of right now, that's certainly the world we're living in. We're looking then for other channels. One of the great channels that we've had good success is our own students. We just did our student satisfaction surveys.

We got the best results that we've had in years, and we're constantly reaching out to our students and say, "Hey, is there someone else, a friend of yours, a cousin, or someone that could benefit from the Lincoln Education just like you are?" That's a very low-cost, I'll say, source of enrollments and leads. We'll constantly look at where is the best value for us to put our time and energy. As I mentioned earlier, we are putting more into social media.

We've recently ensured that every campus, or at least 95% of our campuses, have someone solely dedicated to be on social media, because we know that's where our students are spending a lot of time, and our campuses really have a lot of rich material that is very attractive to people. We're increasing those efforts as well. Again, however we can get out our message is what we're going to pursue, and as the markets change, we'll constantly reallocate our resources accordingly.

Eric Wold: Perfect. Then, follow-up question. I know there's been a big focus on kind of your pre-qualifying, vetting your prospective students ahead of time around the kind of financial aid issues and default issues. Any sense of kind of the number of students or kind of a percentage of students that kind of come looking to enroll and ultimately are unable to because of past financial aid issues?

Scott Shaw: Yeah, I don't have that number, but I can tell you, in general, I mean, it's not something that is of such magnitude that people are viewing that as a headwind for us. I am sure that the number is probably larger than I would like, simply because there's so many people that could benefit from an education. But if they've unfortunately not kept up with their payments, that certainly limits what they can do going forward. But in short, it's not popping up to me at my level as far as being any kind of resistance to our future growth.

Operator: Thank you. Our next question comes from the line of Steven Frankel from Rosenblatt Securities. Your question, please.

Steven Frankel: Good morning, and thank you. Scott, could you talk about show rates? That was one of the factors in last quarter's disappointing start rate. Maybe how show rates changed in Q3 and what you're doing going forward to make sure that they're going in the right direction.

Scott Shaw: Yeah. Well, obviously, we were a little bit surprised in Q2. We obviously didn't want to repeat that. So, we stepped up a number of initiatives. One is just more engagement by our admissions folks with students that are enrolled, just to make sure that they remember the value opportunity and why they selected us and why they want to change their life, and just staying in front of those students so that more of them do start. We definitely had more students start who were enrolled with us. Similarly, it's also with financial aid.

The sooner that the students know how much it's going to cost them and how they're going to pay for the education, the more comfortable they are. Last year, I'm sorry, last quarter, we did have more people than the prior year go through financial aid. This quarter, in third quarter, we had even more people. With the admissions folks supporting that initiative and keeping those students engaged in the process seems to have translated into our start rate was up, frankly, a couple of hundred basis points, which is very impactful.

Steven Frankel: That's great. Then on this ABB effort that you're going to be doing around data centers, could you talk to us about what specifically is in this training that's not in your traditional electrical or HVAC training?

Scott Shaw: Sure. So, in this case, we are actually just helping ABB find people who are graduating from our organization to then enroll at ABB and start their program. It's not requiring, frankly, any additional training by us of our students. It's more finding students that are willing and able to move to locations that ABB has. So, it's really a partnership in placement services for ABB.

Steven Frankel: Great. Thank you so much.

Operator: Thank you. Our next question comes from the line of Eric Martinuzzi from Lake Street Capital Markets. Your question, please.

Eric Martinuzzi: Yeah. I appreciate the upward revision on the revenue side. We didn't get the flow-through, though, to the adjusted EBITDA. Is that back to your comment, Scott, regarding the increased cost of student acquisition?

Scott Shaw: Yeah. I mean, we're no different than anyone else out there. I mean, costs are up kind of across the board in any number of categories. It could be marketing, it could be laptop costs, it could be, frankly, even medical costs. So certain costs are up there, as well as we're continuing, as I mentioned in my remarks, making investments to enhance our experience for our students so that more of them can graduate. We remain about 200 basis points ahead in our retention of our students, and we think that is almost one of the most important metrics that we're looking to drive up. So, we do have some additional investments in that area that are taking place.

But, again, though, you did still see good margin improvement overall for our business. The business model remains the same as we get greater concentration of students at each campus, their profitability increases, for sure.

Eric Martinuzzi: You talk about investments. I see the repurchase program you were very active in the third quarter. Just curious to know, should we anticipate something similar given the share prices at which you were purchasing in Q3 or similar to where we are now? Or is there a, this was opportunistic and we pounced on it, but you guys aren't lacking for places to deploy capital, whether it's building acquisition, new campus investments, debt service. So, what's the-

Eric Martinuzzi: ongoing kind of tempo for repurchases?

Scott Shaw: Sure. I mean, again, it is, we're going to continue to evaluate it. As Brian mentioned in his remarks, and as you just mentioned, we do have a number of growth initiatives underway. And so when we see opportunity and we feel that we have enough liquidity out there to take advantage of it, we and the board will continue to make those decisions. There's nothing written in stone, but as we mentioned, we increased the size of it so that we do have greater flexibility and can take advantage of it when the market seemingly seems to go in a direction that I just don't understand at times.

Operator: Thank you. Our next question comes from the line of Luke Horton from Northland Capital Markets. Your question, please.

Luke Horton: Yeah. Hey, guys. Thanks for taking the questions. Congrats on the quarter.

Luke Horton: Nice to see starts back up double digits here. If we rewind to last quarter, I know there was a lot of uncertainty kind of following the AI search disruptions. I guess, could you just give us a sense of how you feel today versus a few months ago when you reported last quarter, how you feel about that channel? I know you're making some investments in other channels like social media, et cetera, but this one specifically, I guess, how do you feel now versus a few months ago, and any sort of percentage of leads that are coming through an AI search platform that you could help give us some clarity on?

Scott Shaw: Sure. I mean, I'm definitely feeling better simply because our performance is better. It just reassures me that our organization can pivot and we aren't, I'll say, a one-trick pony. We can find other ways to get students. To your primary question, it's still a challenging environment out there because of these AI models. We're certainly not back to anywhere close to where we were six to nine months ago. But I do feel that we are getting a better handle on it, and frankly, the market's probably getting a better handle on it. We're all learning more and figuring out ways how to enhance our presence with these large language models.

But it still remains a bit of a challenge. I'm not going to deny that.

Luke Horton: Okay. Fair enough. Then just kind of switching over to program expansions. You made several over the last couple years. I guess, are there any campuses still left that don't have the core kind of HVAC, electrical, welding courses that you're looking for additional program expansions here in the near term?

Scott Shaw: Yeah. There are no more really for the HVAC and electrical that have, I'll say, space readily available at this moment. I'll just also share this because it's something we're doing. We are expanding our heavy equipment program, which is kind of a spinoff of our diesel program, into Denver and into Grand Prairie, simply because with our increased investment in high school, we believe that there's a good opportunity for high school students who seem to, at least at our Nashville campus, that program is robust with them. And so as we enhance our high school marketing efforts at our other campuses, we think we have an opportunity to grow that program, certainly with the high school workforce.

But as far as other replications, it'll probably be more likely that we'll be replicating some of our healthcare programs in the future once we, I'll say, fully stabilize and get the earnings level that we want from our LPN program, with also that expectation that we are going to continue to pursue the opportunity to have an RN program. And I think that once we have the two, an LPN and RN program, that will become a very attractive replication opportunity for us.

Brian Meyers: The one thing I will add is, as Scott mentioned, at some of our locations, space is at a premium. What we are looking at certain programs that have a little bit lower interest and swapping them out with a higher interest program. Obviously, there will be a slight teach-out associated with that, so we are modeling that out today, but there are several campuses that we might be doing that in the future.

Luke Horton: Okay. Got it. Well, thanks for taking the questions, guys.

Operator: Thank you. Once again, ladies and gentlemen, if you do have a question at this time, please press star 11 on your telephone. This does conclude the question and answer session of today's program. I would like to hand the program back to Scott Shaw for any further remarks.

Scott Shaw: Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today as we reviewed our strong progress. While Lincoln is benefiting from both macro operating environment trends and our own consistent execution of growth initiatives at our existing campuses and new facilities, we are also demonstrating our ability to react quickly and successfully to changing dynamics within the market. The need for skilled trade professionals continues to expand, as does the interest of prospective students to enter a skilled trades profession. Our investments in our operations, our students, and our organization continue to create numerous opportunities to generate increasing levels of shareholder returns over several years.

Of course, our success is only made possible by the commitment and dedication of our faculty and staff and the success of our students. I'd like to thank our shareholders for their support and our entire team for the dedication to achieving our goals. Thank you all again, and have a great day.

Operator: Thank you, ladies and gentlemen, for your participation in today's conference. This does conclude the program. You may now disconnect. Good day.

#3039. WhiteHorse (WHF) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Board forms committee to explore strategic alternatives, including a sale.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

WhiteHorse Finance, Inc. (WHF -3.46%) reported the formation of a special committee to explore strategic alternatives, including a potential sale or corporate transaction for the company. Management indicated that current market conditions in the software sector are providing attractive entry points due to lower enterprise valuations and reduced leverage compared to prior years. The company is prioritizing the monetization of equitized assets, specifically citing active sale processes for Chase Products and Playmonster to transition capital into income-producing investments. The board also declared a special distribution to manage undistributed taxable income while maintaining the base quarterly distribution rate.

Operator: Good afternoon. My name is Chloe, and I will be your conference operator today. At this time, I would like to welcome everyone to the WhiteHorse Finance Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. Our hosts for today's call are Stuart Aronson, Chief Executive Officer; and Joyson Thomas, Chief Financial Officer. Today's call is being recorded, and a replay is available through a webcast in the Investor Relations section of our website at whitehorsefinance.com. [Operator Instructions] It is now my pleasure to turn the call over to [ Rob Munnings ] of Rose & Company.

Unknown Executive: Thanks, Chloe, and thank you, everyone, for joining us today to discuss WhiteHorse Finance's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Results. Before we begin, I would like to remind everyone that certain statements, which are not based on historical facts made during this call, including any statements relating to financial guidance, may be deemed forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Because these forward-looking statements involve known and unknown risks and uncertainties, these are important factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied by these forward-looking statements. WhiteHorse Finance assumes no obligation or responsibility to update any forward-looking statements.

Today's speakers may refer to material from the WhiteHorse Finance Third Quarter 2026 earnings presentation, which was posted to our website earlier today. With that, allow me to introduce WhiteHorse Finance's CEO, Stuart Aronson. Stuart, you may begin.

Stuart Aronson: Thank you, Rob. Good afternoon, everybody. Thank you for joining us today. As you're aware, we issued our earnings this morning before market opened, and I hope you've had a chance to review our results for the period ended September 30, 2026, which can also be found on our website. On today's call, I will begin by addressing our third quarter results, provide a brief update on the actions that both management and our Board have taken to date in creating shareholder value and finally, discuss current market conditions. Then Joyson Thomas, our Chief Financial Officer, will discuss our performance in greater detail, after which we will open the floor for questions.

At a high level, our third quarter results reflected 3 main themes. First, net asset value per share increased for the second consecutive quarter, driven primarily by continued unrealized appreciation and our investments in Chase Products and Playmonster. Two, credit quality improved with the nonaccruals declining to 2% of the debt portfolio at fair value following the restructuring of Outward Hounds. And third, core net investment income increased modestly quarter-over-quarter, while GAAP net investment income saw a decrease relative to the prior quarter as a result of certain nonrecurring noncash expenses and write-offs. Turning to our financial results. Q3 GAAP net investment income was $4.4 million or $0.207 per share and core NII was $4.8 million or $0.224 per share.

This compares with Q2 GAAP net investment income and core NII of $4.7 million or $0.217 per share. The difference between GAAP NII and core NII this quarter reflects approximately $450,000 of nonrecurring expenses or $0.017 per share net of related incentive fee, consisting of the write-off of previously deferred offering costs associated with our shelf registration statement as well as our previously active at-the-market equity offering program. Touching more specifically on the portfolio marks. Net realized and unrealized gains for the quarter were approximately $2.1 million or $0.096 per share.

Net markups were again led by our position in Starco, also known as Chase Products and Pressurized Holdings, where the markup on our equity investment contributed approximately $1.3 million or roughly $0.06 per share. I'll provide more detail on Chase as well and an update on a number of -- and an update on a number of other investments in our portfolio later in the call. NAV per share at the end of Q3 was $11.82 compared with $11.77 at the end of Q2, an increase of approximately 0.4%.

The change in NAV reflected net realized and unrealized gains of approximately $0.09 per share, partially offset by the approximate $0.04 per share NII shortfall as a result of distributions paid during the quarter that exceeded GAAP net investment income for the period. Even though our NII this quarter was below the quarterly distribution rate, as I've shared in the past, we have a number of restructured credits that have been equitized and are not producing meaningful NII. I will discuss and provide updates on a few of these shortly. And to the extent we have realizations on these positions, the reinvested capital should add to the BDC's NII generating capability thereafter. Turning to shareholder value.

As we have discussed on prior calls, both management and the Board remain focused on actions that we believe can help enhance shareholder value over time. This focus has included disciplined portfolio repositioning, selective capital deployment, accretive share repurchases and steps to support distributable earnings. Cumulatively, since the inception of our share repurchase program in the fourth quarter of 2025, we have repurchased approximately 1.8 million shares at a weighted average price of approximately $7.36 per share, and we estimate that our buybacks have contributed approximately $0.33 per share to NAV accretion.

Additionally, over that same time frame, the BDC's adviser has agreed to voluntary incentive fee waiver, reducing the applicable rate from 20% to 17.5% Cumulatively, this aggregates to approximately $530,000 or approximately $0.024 per share in the incentive fees waived by the adviser in an effort to support distributable earnings. The adviser has again agreed to extend voluntary incentive fee waiver for the fourth quarter of 2026, reducing the applicable rate from 20% to 17.5%.

Now as an extension of our commitment to seeking ways to create shareholder value and as previously announced on September 15, our Board has formed a special committee of independent directors to explore strategic alternatives for the company, which could include a sale or other strategic alternative for the company -- sorry, which could include a sale or other corporate transaction. That review is ongoing. The special committee has not set a timetable for the conclusion of its review, and there can be no assurance that the review will result in the company pursuing or completing any transaction.

Consistent with our prior announcement, we do not intend to comment further on the review unless and until the special committee has approved its definitive course of action or the review is concluded or it is otherwise determined that further disclosure is appropriate or required by law. Accordingly, we will not be taking questions on the strategic review during today's call. Turning to our portfolio activity. We had gross capital deployments of $21 million in Q3. Repayments and sales totaled approximately $10 million, resulting in net deployments of approximately $10.9 million before the effects of transferring assets into the STRS JV.

Gross capital deployments consisted of 2 new originations totaling $14.8 million, with the remaining $6.2 million deployed to fund add-ons to existing portfolio companies. The 2 new originations were Transervice Logistics for $8 million, which refinanced our existing investment in that company and KORE Wireless Group for $6.8 million, which was transferred into the STRS JV during the quarter. Add-on fundings were led by Motiva Group at $2.6 million and Kelso Industries at $1.7 million. Of our 2 new originations in Q3, one was nonsponsor and one was sponsor. New originations in Q3 had an average leverage of only 3.6x EBITDA and were all first lien loans.

Total repayments and sales of $10 million were driven primarily by the repayment of our prior Transervice Logistics term loan of $7.6 million, which generated a gross IRR of 14.6% as well as the realization of our residual equity position in PFB for $0.2 million. During the quarter, the BDC transferred 5 deals to the STRS JV totaling $21.4 million. The transfers were headlined by KORE Wireless of $6.8 million intermediate cloud communications of $6.6 million and vibration mountings and controls of $6.3 million. We continue to successfully utilize the STRS JV and believe that WhiteHorse Finance equity investment in the JV continues to provide attractive returns to our shareholders.

After net deployments and JV transfer activity as well as net realized and unrealized gains recognized during the quarter, total investments were essentially unchanged at $569.1 million. During the quarter, we recognized approximately $3.6 million in net realized losses driven by the restructuring of Outward Hound and approximately $5.7 million of net unrealized gains, which included $4.1 million from Outward Hound, driven by the reversal of $3.8 million in previously unrecognized previously recognized unrealized depreciation for aggregate net realized and unrealized gains of approximately $2.1 million or approximately $0.096 per share.

The net gains included a $1.3 million markup on Chase, a $0.7 million markup on Playmonster and approximately $0.8 million of other net markups across the portfolio, which were partially offset by a $0.7 million markdown on Arcserve. As a reminder, Chase Products is a developer and manufacturer of bulk consumer and industrial chemical and aerosol products in the United States. The company continues to perform ahead of plan and the markup this quarter reflects the continued improvement. We are now in active sale process for Chase. To date, that process has generated constructive indications of interest from buyers and we currently expect the sale to be completed in the next 2 to 4 months.

As always, there can be no assurance as to the timing or outcome of that process. Playmonster, as you may recall, is a toy and game company with owned and licensed brands, including Hacky Sack, Spirograph, Taco vs. Burrito and 5-second Rule. The business has experienced a material resurgence in demand across multiple products in its portfolio, which is driving strong performance and the markup this quarter reflects that trajectory. Based on that strong performance, we believe there could be a likelihood that a sale of the company is pursued in the first half of 2027.

Both positions generate limited cash income today, a realization in either case would convert the full realized value into cash available for future redeployment into income-producing investments which would positively contribute to helping to support core NII over time. Regarding [ Arc Share ], the markdown on our position this quarter reflects several quarters of relative weakness in the business. The company remains cash flow positive, though, and we are working with the management team on initiatives to accelerate growth. More broadly, as reflected in our remarks, a small number of credits are experiencing relative softness. In most of those cases, the owners are supporting the companies with additional equity.

Across the portfolio, the average credit has been stable to improving. At the end of Q3, 98.8% of our debt portfolio was first lien and senior secured, and our portfolio continued to reflect a balanced mix of sponsor and nonsponsor investments with nonsponsor representing approximately 42% of the portfolio at fair value. The weighted average effective yield on the income-producing debt investments was 11% at the end of Q3 compared with 10.8% at the end of Q2. The weighted average effective yield on our overall portfolio was approximately 8.7% at the end of Q3 compared to approximately 8.8% at the end of Q2.

With respect to nonaccrual status, the restructured Outward Hound term loan returned to accrual status during the quarter, and there were no new additions to nonaccrual. Excluding the SGRS JV nonaccrual investments, represented 2% of the total debt portfolio at fair value compared with 3.6% at the end of the prior quarter and 4.4% at cost compared with 6.9% of cost at the end of the prior quarter. Investments in 3 issuers remain on nonaccrual at quarter end, which were Camarillo Fitness, New Cycle Solutions and Playmonster. Turning to Outward Hound. We completed the restructuring of the business in early July. Alongside the other lenders, we were recapitalized the company and converted a portion of the restructured debt into equity.

WhiteHorse now holds majority ownership and control of the Board. The pet products market remains challenging, and we are working with management on initiatives to grow revenues and reduce costs. Finally, regarding Camarillo Fitness, formerly known as Honors Holdings, our mark reflects the expected proceeds from the sale of the underlying locations. That process is actively underway. And as locations are sold and cash is returned, we will redeploy that capital into income-producing investments. As always, we continue to actively manage underperforming credits, leveraging our dedicated restructuring resources, which is a team of 5 people and the broad capabilities of H.I.G. Aside from the credits on nonaccrual and those I have mentioned, our portfolio continues to perform well.

Our exposure to software companies remains modest at approximately 10.9% of the portfolio at cost and 9.3% of the portfolio at fair value across 6 portfolio companies. Now turning to the market. Over the course of 2026, the negative press surrounding the direct lending industry, together with outflows of retail capital has contributed to more rational risk return environment in general. We are seeing lenders take a more conservative approach to add-backs, synergies and run rate adjustments. Deal structures are generally back below 55% loan-to-value and cash flow coverage is solid and pricing for most of the 2026 vintage has been 50 to 75 basis points higher than in 2025 and 2024.

Because many lenders are overallocated to software and unable to consider new deals in that sector, the software opportunities we are now seeing are unusually attractive with lower enterprise value, lower loan-to-value, much lower leverage and pricing that is 100 to 150 basis points higher than for an equivalent deal outside of the software sector. Given our historically low concentration in software, we are considering some of these opportunities. Consistent with historical practice, we will continue to manage overall sector concentration in a conservative manner. The nonsponsor market remains stable, although we are seeing fewer nonsponsored deals at the moment.

Nonsponsor deals continue to be structured at 3 to 4.5x leverage with pricing of SOFR plus 600 and above and covenant protection. Reflecting the more conservative market, we are also getting covenants on the vast majority of our sponsor deals. In general, we are finding 2026 to be a constructive credit market. Volumes across WhiteHorse platform are up in its estimated 50% or more over the 2025 levels, which is making more assets available to the BDC to the extent there is capacity. Subsequent to quarter end, the company closed on one new sponsor investment of approximately $65 million and the STRS JV closed on one new sponsor investment of approximately $4.9 million.

We have also received full repayments of our debt investment in Quest Events and the unrealized equity co-investment is still held at the BDC on its balance sheet. Pro forma for Q4 activity, the STRS JV has capacity of approximately $22 million of additional assets and the BDC balance sheet has capacity for approximately $25 million. We will continue to create additional capacity as we receive repayments on other deals. With that, I'll turn the call over to Joyson for additional performance details and a review of our portfolio composition. Joyson?

Joyson Thomas: Thanks, Stuart, and thank you, everyone, for joining today's call. During the quarter, we recorded GAAP net investment income of $4.4 million or $0.207 per share and core NII of $4.8 million or $0.224 per share. This compares with Q2 GAAP NII and core NII of $4.7 million or $0.217 per share, as well as our previously declared third quarter base distribution of $0.25 per share. Stuart mentioned, core NII excludes approximately $450,000 of nonrecurring expenses related to our shelf registration statements and ATM program or $0.017 per share net of the related incentive fee.

Q3 fee income was approximately $0.2 million compared with $0.1 million in the prior quarter, driven primarily by an amendment fee from Future Payment Technologies of approximately $0.1 million. Total expenses for the quarter were $10.4 million compared with $9.7 million in the prior quarter. The increase was driven primarily by the nonrecurring expenses I just mentioned, as well as approximately $0.1 million of independent director fees related to the special committee. For the quarter, we reported a net increase in net assets resulting from operations of $6.5 million. Our risk ratings during the quarter showed that approximately 84.8% of our portfolio positions either carried a 1 or 2 rating, slightly lower than the 86.6% reported in the prior quarter.

As a reminder, a 1 rating indicates that a company has seen its risk of loss reduced relative to initial expectations and a 2 rating indicates the company is performing according to such initial expectations. Regarding the JV specifically, we continue to utilize the platform as a complement to the BDC. As Stuart mentioned earlier, we transferred 5 deals during the third quarter to the STRS JV totaling $21.4 million in exchange for a net investment in the STRS JV of $7.2 million as well as cash proceeds of approximately $14.2 million. With that activity, the remaining capital commitments to the JV were fully called during the quarter. During the quarter, there were 3 full realizations in the JV.

At the end of Q3, the STRS JV's total portfolio had an aggregate fair value of $332.6 million across 43 issuers, of which 14 are common issuers with the company and an average effective yield of approximately 9.9%. This compares with an aggregate fair value of $340.3 million and an average effective yield of approximately 9.8% across 43 portfolio companies as of June 30. Leverage for the JV at the end of Q3 was approximately 0.93x compared with approximately 1.10x at the end of the prior quarter. The investment in the JV continues to be accretive to the BDC's earnings, generating a low teens return on equity.

During Q3, income recognized from our JV investment aggregated to approximately $3.5 million compared to approximately $3.2 million reported in Q2. As we have noted in prior calls, the yield on our investment in the JV may fluctuate period-over-period as a result of a number of factors, including the timing and amount of additional capital investments, changes in asset yields in the underlying portfolio and the overall credit performance of the JV's investment portfolio. Turning to our balance sheet.

We had cash resources of approximately $23.1 million at the end of Q3, including approximately $16 million in restricted cash, representing interest and principal proceeds received during the quarter in our securitized leverage facilities and approximately $7.1 million at the fund level held for expenses in the quarterly dividend paid in early October. As a reminder, we have $85 million of unsecured notes maturing in December of this year, consisting of $10 million of our 5.375% notes due December 4 and $75 million of our 4% notes due December 15. We are actively working to address these maturities and are in discussions regarding a financing solution.

Based on the progress to date, we feel good about our ability to address these maturities when due, but are not in a position to provide further details at this time. As of September 30, 2026, the company's asset coverage ratio for borrowed amounts as defined by the 1940 Act was 177.3%, which is above the minimum asset coverage ratio of 150%. At quarter end, gross leverage was 1.29x compared with 1.30x in the prior quarter, while our net effective debt-to-equity ratio after adjusting for cash on hand was 1.20x compared with 1.19x in the prior quarter. The modest increase in net effective leverage primarily reflected lower cash balances at quarter end.

As Stuart mentioned earlier, the adviser has agreed to extend the temporary voluntary incentive fee waiver for the fourth quarter of 2026, reducing the applicable rate from 20% to 17.5%. We view the fee waiver as a constructive step to support distributable earnings and shareholder value. As we have said previously, this irrevocable fee waiver is temporary and any decision regarding future periods will be revisited based on the then current conditions and in consultation with our Board. Before I conclude and open up the call to questions, I'd like to discuss our recent distributions and corresponding distribution policy. This morning, we announced that our Board declared a fourth quarter base distribution of $0.25 per share.

The distribution will be payable on January 6, 2027, to stockholders of record as of December 21, 2026. In addition to our quarterly distribution, we elected to declare a special distribution of $0.17 per share for stockholders of record as of October 30, 2026. The distribution will be payable on December 10, 2026. The distribution was related to undistributed taxable income that was earned last year, which would have otherwise been taxable. Pro forma for distributions paid this year and including the special distribution, we estimate our current spillback income to be approximately $14.3 million.

As we've said previously, we will continue to evaluate our quarterly distribution, both in the near and medium term based on the core earnings power of our portfolio in addition to other relevant factors that may warrant consideration. With that, I'll now turn the call back over to the operator for your questions. Operator?

So we actually would have been paid or would need to have been paid by the end of this year. In regards to your question on liquidity as well as the maturities, so you're absolutely right that we would not necessarily have declared the special distribution that we thought we would need that liquidity for purposes of the maturities coming due in December.

As we've mentioned in our prior earnings call, we do have capacity under our existing JPM credit facility as well as some additional cash on hand. And we've been actively monitoring both the public and private debt markets and have been speaking actively with a number of lenders on a financing solution, as I just mentioned. As I said before, we feel very optimistic and very comfortable with where we are right now relative to the maturities next month.

Richard Shane: Got it. And then just as we think about this -- and again, look, I realize there is nuance to being able to answer this. But if you can give us sort of a generic sense of how much you think the market is -- last approach, that would be helpful.

Stuart Aronson: At least for me, Rob, you looked out during the question. So give at least a sense of something.

Richard Shane: Sorry. And then you dipped out like you were asking me to repeat my question. I was asking sort of how much -- obviously, that's very low-cost funding. It's very attractive. Joyson Thomas: What I would tell you is if you look at the vintages of those debt issuances, they were 2021 or before, right? And so with respect to that and including that $75 million 4% issuance, we're not necessarily going to see those types of rates. If you look at kind of the current retail environment for BDCs of comparable size, they've been obviously over 7% on a fixed rate basis, probably 7.5% to somewhere between 7% to 8%, I would say. As I mentioned before and as you alluded to as well, the ABL facility does provide some attractive cost to us, and we have a bit of capacity to draw on those amounts.

Stuart Aronson: Yes. The technology or software deals that we've seen really fit into 2 categories. Category 1 is people trying to fix broken capital structures. Stuart Aronson: No, not at all. We don't know if the strategic options will result in a successful transaction. And not knowing that, we continue to reinvest the portfolio carefully and selectively in a market environment that is really the best market environment here in 2026 that we've seen in about 3 or 4 years, 3 years probably. And we're seeing solid credits, good capital structures, good documents with covenant protection and pricing that on average is 50 to 75 basis points better than it was last year. So the main issue in the market, even though our volumes will be up year-over-year at WhiteHorse is that M&A activity is not that strong.

And Q3, I think, was flat to down from last year in the market. And I expect when the Q4 numbers come out, they'll also show a decrease in M&A activity. That said, we have about 20 originators in 11 physical locations across North America, and that helps us gin up deals outside of the normal sponsor M&A flow. And we hope to get some interesting deals done, hopefully in Q4 and/or early in Q1.

Joyson Thomas: Chris, I was just going to add to that. When we paused the share buyback in Q2, I think it reflects Stuart's comments just now where, again, as we do buybacks, that reduces our equity. And so we need to balance that with putting capital back to work and deploying that into newly originated investments. So it's obviously a fine balance.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Thank you. It does appear that there are no further questions at this time. This brings us to the end of today's meeting. We appreciate your time and participation. You may now disconnect.
